definition_zh: 忠实地；如实地；尽职地；（信末）谨启
definition_en: in a loyal and dependable way; accurately and true to the facts; dutifully over time; used to close a formal letter when the reader's name is unknown
core_image: 每一年都按时守约，从不缺席
scene: 他忠实地履行了自己的职责。 He faithfully carried out his duties.
sceneCN: 这里 faithfully 是「忠实地、尽职地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他忠实地履行了自己的职责。

derivatives.zh: 忠诚的；忠实的
忠诚；忠实
不忠的；不准确的

senses.title: Loyally
senses.definition: in a loyal and dependable way toward a person or cause
senses.definitionCN: 以忠诚可靠的方式对待人或事业
senses.example: She served the charity faithfully for years.
senses.exampleCN: 她多年来忠实地为这家慈善机构服务。
senses.why: The base sense is steady loyalty in action.
senses.whyCN: 基础义是行动中稳定的忠诚。

senses.title: Accurately
senses.definition: accurately and true to the facts or the original
senses.definitionCN: 准确并忠实于事实或原作
senses.example: The report faithfully records what happened.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告如实记录了所发生的事。
senses.why: Loyalty to a person extends to loyalty to truth.
senses.whyCN: 对人的忠诚延伸到对真相的忠诚。

senses.title: Dutifully
senses.definition: with steady attention to duty over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 长期稳定地尽责
senses.example: He faithfully attended every meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 他每次会议都尽职参加。
senses.why: Repeated loyalty becomes reliability.
senses.whyCN: 反复的忠诚变成可靠。

senses.title: A formal letter closing
senses.definition: used at the end of a formal letter when the reader's name is unknown
senses.definitionCN: 用于不知道收信人姓名的正式信件结尾
senses.example: The letter ended with yours faithfully.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信以「谨启」结尾。
senses.why: The closing promises loyal respect to the reader.
senses.whyCN: 结尾套语向收信人许诺忠诚的敬意。

intro.en: Faithfully is faithful plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: faithfully 由 faithful 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Fides means trust and loyalty.
items.cn: fides 意为信任与忠诚。

items.en: Feid carries the sense of faithfulness.
items.cn: feid 带有忠诚之义。

items.en: Faithful means full of loyalty.
items.cn: 中古英语中 faithful 意为充满忠诚。

items.en: Yours faithfully becomes a letter formula.
items.cn: 早期现代英语中 yours faithfully 成为书信套语。

items.en: Faithfully also means accurately.
items.cn: 现代英语中 faithfully 也指如实、准确。

note.en: Faithfully means loyally; fatefully means with great consequence.
note.cn: faithfully 是忠实地，fatefully 则是决定性地。

entries.definition: loyal and true
entries.definitionCN: 忠诚的

entries.definition: not loyal
entries.definitionCN: 不忠的

entries.definition: with important consequences
entries.definitionCN: 决定性地

entries.definition: in a correct and exact way
entries.definitionCN: 准确地

entries.definition: in a way that shows duty
entries.definitionCN: 尽职地

normalIntro.en: Faithfully applies faithful to an action, from service to reporting.
normalIntro.cn: faithfully 把 faithful 用于动作，从服务到报道。

normal.en: The dog waited faithfully by the door.
normal.cn: 狗忠实地守在门边。

normal.en: The translation faithfully keeps the original tone.
normal.cn: 译文忠实地保留了原文语气。

normal.en: He faithfully followed the doctor's advice.
normal.cn: 他忠实遵照医生的建议。

normal.en: She has faithfully kept a diary for years.
normal.cn: 她多年来坚持写日记。

normal.en: End the letter with yours faithfully.
normal.cn: 信末用「谨启」结束。

abstract.en: Picture a guard who never leaves the gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一名从不离开岗位的守卫。

abstract.en: Imagine a copy that keeps every detail.
abstract.cn: 想象一份保留每个细节的复制品。

abstract.en: Think of a habit repeated every day for years.
abstract.cn: 想象多年如一日重复的习惯。

examples.en: The staff faithfully carried out the plan.
examples.cn: 员工们忠实地执行了计划。

examples.en: The novel was faithfully adapted for the screen.
examples.cn: 这部小说被忠实地改编成电影。

examples.en: Please write yours faithfully at the end.
examples.cn: 请在末尾写上「谨启」。

dict_mnemonic.note: 构词记忆 · 双层后缀

branches.en: The base sense is loyal action.
branches.cn: 基础义是忠诚的行动。

branches.en: Loyalty to truth means accuracy.
branches.cn: 对真相的忠诚就是准确。

branches.en: Repeated loyalty becomes duty.
branches.cn: 反复的忠诚成为尽责。

branches.en: The letter closing promises loyal respect.
branches.cn: 书信结尾承诺忠诚的敬意。

branches.en: Service and reporting both require fidelity.
branches.cn: 服务与报道都要求忠实。

intro.en: Faithfully combines the suffix -ful with the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: faithfully 把后缀 -ful 与副词词尾 -ly 结合起来。

latinIntro.en: The word inherits Latin fides through French forms.
latinIntro.cn: 该词经由法语形式继承拉丁语 fides。

items.exampleCN: 他如实回答了所有问题。
不实的记述会误导读者。

items.exampleCN: 不知道对方姓名时用「谨启」。

items.example: The letter closed with faithfully yours.

latinEntries.example: Fides is the root of faithfully.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fides 是 faithfully 的词根。

definition_zh: 谣言；传闻；谣传
definition_en: an unverified story spread from person to person; general talk about something; to spread something as gossip
core_image: 一句未经证实的话在人群里悄悄传开
scene: 关于公司裁员的谣言迅速传开。 The rumour about job cuts spread quickly.
sceneCN: 这里 rumour 是「谣言、传闻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：关于公司裁员的谣言迅速传开。

derivatives.zh: 传闻的；据说的
传言渠道；流言圈
散布谣言者

senses.title: Unverified story
senses.definition: an unverified story spread from person to person
senses.definitionCN: 在人与人之间传播的未经证实的故事
senses.example: There is a rumour that the factory will close.
senses.exampleCN: 有传闻说工厂将要关闭。
senses.why: The core sense is talk without proof.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是没有证据的说法。

senses.title: General talk
senses.definition: general talk about something, often unkind
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事的普遍议论，常带恶意
senses.example: Rumour spread through the village.
senses.exampleCN: 流言在村里传开了。
senses.why: One story becomes a wave of talk.
senses.whyCN: 一个说法变成一片议论。

senses.title: To spread as gossip
senses.definition: to spread something as gossip
senses.definitionCN: 把某事当作流言传播
senses.example: He is rumoured to be leaving.
senses.exampleCN: 据传他要离开。
senses.why: The noun becomes the act of spreading talk.
senses.whyCN: 名词变成传播说法的动作。

intro.en: Rumour comes from Latin rumor, noise or common talk.
intro.cn: rumour 源自拉丁语 rumor，意为喧哗或众人议论。

items.en: Rumor means noise or common talk.
items.cn: rumor 意为喧哗或众人议论。

items.en: Rumour keeps the sense of talk.

items.en: Rumour names unconfirmed news.

items.en: Rumour has it is a fixed phrase.
items.cn: rumour has it 成为固定说法。

note.en: A rumour is unproven talk; a report is a formal account.
note.cn: rumour 是未经证实的传言，report 则是正式报道。

entries.definition: the American spelling of rumour

entries.definition: information heard from others

normalIntro.en: A rumour is talk that travels before the facts.
normalIntro.cn: rumour 是跑在事实前面的说法。

normal.en: The rumour spread faster than the news.
normal.cn: 谣言的传播比新闻还快。

normal.en: He is rumoured to have left the country.

normal.en: Do not repeat a rumour you cannot prove.

abstract.cn: 想象一句耳语沿着一排座位传下去。

abstract.en: Imagine a paper note folded and passed hand to hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸条被一只手传到另一只手。

abstract.en: Think of smoke that grows as it drifts.

examples.cn: 关于合并的传闻传到了媒体那里。

examples.en: It is rumoured that the coach will resign.

sensesIntro.en: Rumour means an unverified story, general talk, or to spread something as gossip.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a whisper moving from ear to ear.

branches.en: The base sense is an unproven story.

definition_zh: 火箭；烟火；迅速上升
definition_en: a vehicle or firework driven upward by burning fuel, or to rise very fast
core_image: 拖着白烟冲向天空的火箭
scene: 倒计时结束，火箭拖着白烟冲向天空。 The countdown ended and the rocket shot into the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 rocket 是「火箭」（第 1 个义项：靠燃烧燃料升空的飞行器）；句意：倒计时结束，火箭拖着白烟冲向天空。

derivatives.zh: 火箭学；火箭技术
火箭专家；火箭操作者

senses.title: A space vehicle
senses.definition: a vehicle driven upward by burning fuel
senses.definitionCN: 靠燃烧燃料向上推进的飞行器
senses.example: The rocket carried a small satellite.
senses.exampleCN: 这枚火箭运载了一颗小卫星。
senses.why: Burning fuel pushes the craft against gravity.
senses.whyCN: 燃烧的燃料把飞行器推向重力之上。

senses.title: A firework or signal
senses.definition: a firework that shoots up or a warning flare
senses.definitionCN: 冲上天空的烟火或警示信号弹
senses.example: A red rocket marked the start of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 一枚红色信号弹标志着比赛开始。
senses.why: The old firework is a small rocket.
senses.whyCN: 古老的烟火就是一枝小火箭。

senses.title: Rising fast
senses.definition: to increase or move upward very quickly
senses.definitionCN: 非常迅速地增长或向上移动
senses.example: House prices rocketed last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 去年春天房价飞涨。
senses.why: A rocket's climb becomes a picture of speed.
senses.whyCN: 火箭的爬升成为速度的图景。

examples.en: A warning rocket lit the night sky.

examples.en: Demand for the new phone rocketed.

items.example: Rocket entered English as a firework.

definition_zh: 耐用的；持久的；耐久的
definition_en: able to last a long time without breaking or wearing out, or continuing for a long time without fading
core_image: 一双走过泥地与碎石、鞋底却仍未开裂的旧靴
scene: 那双旧靴子走过泥地和碎石，鞋底边缘只是磨白了一点。 These boots are durable enough for daily work.
sceneCN: 这里 durable 是「耐用的」（第 1 个义项：经得起长期使用而不损坏）；句意是这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。

pos.zh: 形容词：耐用的；持久的；耐久的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「耐久性；耐用性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「耐久地；持久地」
与 durable 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「持续时间；时长」

senses.title: Able to last without breaking
senses.definition: made to last a long time and to resist wear, pressure or damage
senses.definitionCN: 经得起长时间使用，能抵抗磨损、压力或损坏
senses.example: These boots are durable enough for daily work.
senses.exampleCN: 这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。
senses.why: Latin durare meant to last, so durable describes an object that keeps its shape under use.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 durare 意为「持续」，所以 durable 形容一件在反复使用中仍能保持原形的物品。

senses.title: Continuing for a long time
senses.definition: lasting a long time without fading, weakening or ending, as a peace or a relationship
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续而不消退、不减弱、不终结，如和平或关系
senses.example: The two countries signed a durable peace agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 两国签署了一份持久的和平协议。
senses.why: The same 'lasting' quality is applied to agreements and feelings, where what must resist wear is time rather than friction.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「耐久」品质被用到协议与感情上，那里要抵抗磨损的不是摩擦，而是时间。

senses.title: Goods that last, in economics
senses.definition: used of goods, such as cars or washing machines, that are expected to be used for several years
senses.definitionCN: 用于汽车、洗衣机等预期可使用数年的商品
senses.example: Durable goods such as washing machines are taxed differently.
senses.exampleCN: 洗衣机等耐用品的征税方式有所不同。
senses.why: Economists needed a label for goods that survive many uses, and the adjective became a fixed category.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家需要给能经受多次使用的商品一个标签，这个形容词于是成了固定类别。

intro.en: Durable comes from Latin durare, to last, through Old French; the whole family also gives duration and endure.
intro.cn: durable 经由古法语来自拉丁语 durare（持续），同一词族还给出 duration 与 endure。

items.en: Latin durus meant hard, firm or tough, and it is the adjective behind the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 durus 意为「坚硬的、结实的」，是整个词族背后的形容词。

items.en: The verb durare meant to last, to endure or to remain hard, and it supplied the idea of continuing through time.
items.cn: 动词 durare 意为「持续、忍耐、保持坚硬」，提供了「贯穿时间而延续」的观念。

items.en: The adjective durabilis meant lasting or durable and passed into French as durable.
items.cn: 形容词 durabilis 意为「持久的、耐久的」，后来进入法语作 durable。

items.en: Old French durable carried the sense of lasting and resisting wear into English.
items.cn: 古法语 durable 把「持久、抗磨损」的含义带进了英语。

items.en: Middle English durable was used for materials and for promises that were meant to hold.
items.cn: 中古英语 durable 用于材料，也用于本当守住的承诺。

items.en: Economics fixed durable goods as a category, while ordinary speech kept durable for anything that survives hard use.
items.cn: 经济学把 durable goods 固定为类别，日常语言则用 durable 形容任何经得起折腾的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin lasting family; the near-meaning group separates lasting, sturdy and tough by what they resist.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「持续」词族的词；近义组按所抵抗的对象区分 lasting、sturdy 与 tough。

entries.definition: The quality of lasting or resisting wear; durable plus -ity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耐久性、耐用性」，由 durable 加 -ity 构成。

entries.definition: In a lasting or durable manner; durable plus -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「耐久地、持久地」，由 durable 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The length of time something continues; from Latin durare.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「持续时间、时长」，来自拉丁语 durare。

entries.definition: To suffer something or to last through it; from Latin indurare, related to durus.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「忍受、持续」，来自与 durus 相关的拉丁语 indurare。

entries.definition: Continuing for a long time; close to durable but with less emphasis on resistance to wear.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「持久的」，接近 durable，但较少强调抗磨损。

entries.definition: Strong and solidly built; it stresses resistance to force more than length of use.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「结实的」，更强调抗外力而非使用年限。

entries.definition: Not easily broken or damaged; broader and more informal than durable.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚韧的」，比 durable 更宽泛、更口语。

entries.definition: Able to recover shape or strength after pressure; it stresses bounce-back, not just survival.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有弹性的、能恢复的」，强调受压迫后回弹，而不只是撑住。

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect Latin durare, to last, with boots, peace treaties and durable goods.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子把拉丁语 durare（持续）与靴子、和平协议和耐用品连在一起。

normal.en: Latin durare is to last, so durable means able to keep going.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 durare 是「持续」，所以 durable 就是「能一直撑下去」。

normal.en: Durability is the noun, durably the adverb: the family keeps the same idea.
normal.cn: durability 是名词，durably 是副词，这一族保留同一个观念。

normal.en: The same root gives duration, which is time lasting, and endure, which is lasting through hardship.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 duration（持续的时间）与 endure（熬过艰难而持续）。

normal.en: A durable boot survives mud; a durable peace survives years.
normal.cn: 耐用的靴子熬过泥泞，持久的和平熬过岁月。

normal.en: Durable goods are things a household expects to keep for years, not weeks.
normal.cn: 耐用品是家庭预期会用上几年而不是几周的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a boot sole that has crossed the same gravel for ten years and still holds its shape.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鞋底在同一片碎石上走了十年，仍然保持原形。

abstract.en: Draw the same line under a peace treaty: the paper is thin, but the agreement does not wear through.
abstract.cn: 把同一条线画在一份和平协议下：纸很薄，协议却没有被磨穿。

abstract.en: Durable is about time failing to break something, whether it is leather, metal or a promise.
abstract.cn: durable 讲的是时间没能弄坏某物，无论那是皮革、金属还是一个承诺。

examples.en: These boots are durable enough for daily work.
examples.cn: 这双靴子足够耐用，适合日常干活。

examples.en: The two countries signed a durable peace agreement.
examples.cn: 两国签署了一份持久的和平协议。

examples.en: Durable goods such as washing machines are taxed differently.
examples.cn: 洗衣机等耐用品的征税方式有所不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: dur- 是「坚硬、持续」：durable 是经得住用的，duration 是持续的时间，endure 是熬得住。

root: 经由古法语 durable 来自拉丁语 durabilis，后者由 durare「持续、忍耐」加 -abilis 构成；durare 又源于 durus「坚硬的、结实的」。同一词根还给出 duration、endure、durability。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses of durable apply one idea of lasting to an object, to an agreement, and to a category of goods.
sensesIntro.cn: durable 的三个义项把同一个「持久」观念分别用到物品、协议和一类商品上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn boot whose sole still holds together after years of gravel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双磨旧的靴子，鞋底在多年碎石之后仍然完好。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a material or product that resists wear and pressure.
branches.cn: 物品线：抵抗磨损与压力的材料或产品。

branches.en: THE BOND: an agreement or relationship that time does not wear through.
branches.cn: 纽带线：时间磨不穿的协议或关系。

branches.en: THE MARKET: a class of goods expected to serve for years.
branches.cn: 市场线：预期能使用多年的一类商品。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF WEAR: leather resists friction, while a promise resists time.
branches.cn: 两种磨损：皮革抵抗摩擦，承诺抵抗时间。

branches.en: THE LONG USE: durability is what turns an object into a long-term purchase.
branches.cn: 长期使用线：耐久性使一件物品成为长期投资。

intro.en: Durable is a Latin-derived adjective built from a verb root plus -able; English adds -ity and -ly.
intro.cn: durable 是源自拉丁语的形容词，由动词词根加 -able 构成；英语再加 -ity 与 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin durus, durare and durabilis are all recorded, so only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 durus、durare、durabilis 均有记录，只有更早的印欧语词根属于重构。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of resistance.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供「抵抗」的观念。

items.example: It is the adjective behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 它是这一词族背后的形容词。
它提供时间层面的含义。

items.meaning: able to be or to do
items.example: It forms durabilis and English durable.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拉丁语 durabilis 与英语 durable。

items.example: It forms duration from the same root.

items.exampleCN: 它与 durus 共享词根。

latinEntries.meaning: to last, to endure, to remain hard

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「耐久性；耐用性」
由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「耐久地；持久地」
与 durable 同出拉丁语 durare，义为「持续时间；时长」

definition_zh: 擦；擦净；抹去；（引申）消除；抹掉
definition_en: to clean or dry a surface by passing a cloth or the hand over it, and to remove something in that motion
core_image: 一只手拿着湿布从桌子一端抹到另一端，水痕和 crumbs 一起被推到桌角
scene: 饭后，他把湿布往桌上一铺，从这头抹到那头，汤渍和碎屑一起被推到桌角。 She wiped the table twice before the guests arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 wipe 是「擦、擦净」（第 1 个义项：用布或手在表面抹过使之洁净）；句意为客人到达前她把桌子擦了两遍。湿布从桌子一头推到另一头那道弧线，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 擦拭者；雨刷
擦拭
彻底失败；全灭
湿纸巾

senses.title: To clean a surface
senses.definition: to pass a cloth over a surface to clean or dry it
senses.definitionCN: 用布在表面抹过，使之干净或干燥
senses.example: She wiped the table twice before the guests arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 客人到达前她把桌子擦了两遍。
senses.why: The oldest sense is a single sweeping movement of the hand over something, and cleaning came with it.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项是手在某物上一道抹过，洁净之义随这道动作而来。

senses.title: To remove by rubbing
senses.definition: to take something off a surface with a cloth or the hand, such as liquid, dust or tears
senses.definitionCN: 用布或手把液体、灰尘或眼泪从表面上带走
senses.example: He wiped the mud off his boots at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口把靴子上的泥擦掉。
senses.why: Once the movement cleans, the thing carried away becomes the point: what is wiped is gone.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这道动作能清洁，被带走的东西就成了重点：被擦掉的就是没了。

senses.title: To destroy completely
senses.definition: in phrases such as wipe out, to remove something entirely, sometimes with great violence
senses.definitionCN: 在 wipe out 等说法中，指把某物完全除去，有时指猛烈毁灭
senses.example: The flood wiped out the village's only bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水冲毁了村里唯一的一座桥。
senses.why: If a cloth can make a mark disappear, then a force can make a whole thing disappear in the same image.
senses.whyCN: 既然一块布能让痕迹消失，那么一股力量也能用同样的画面让整个东西消失。

senses.title: The act of wiping
senses.definition: a single movement with a cloth, used as a countable noun
senses.definitionCN: 用布抹一次的动作，作可数名词
senses.example: A quick wipe with a dry cloth will do.
senses.exampleCN: 用干布快速擦一下就行。
senses.why: The noun simply names the movement that the verb performs.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是命名动词所做的那个动作。

intro.en: Wipe is a Germanic word of movement, first recorded in Old English as wipian, to rub or clean a surface.
intro.cn: wipe 是日耳曼语中表示动作的词，古英语里最先记为 wipian，意为擦、拭净表面。

items.en: wipian meant to rub or wipe something clean, often with a cloth.
items.cn: wipian 表示摩擦或把某物擦净，常用布来做。

items.en: The word kept the same body but gained the phrasal partners off and away.
items.cn: 这个词形式未变，却获得了 off、away 这样的介词伙伴。

items.en: To wipe away tears appears early, extending the verb from objects to the face.
items.cn: 擦去眼泪的用法很早就出现，把这个动词从物件扩展到了脸。

items.en: Wipe out, meaning to destroy utterly, spread through war reporting and later sport.
items.cn: 表示彻底摧毁的 wipe out 通过战地报道传播，后来又进入体育。

items.en: Cleaners and machines gave the noun new life, from windscreen wipers to wet wipes.
items.cn: 清洁用品与机器给名词带来新生命，从雨刷到湿纸巾。

note.en: The first group holds short look-alikes, the second verbs of cleaning and removing.
note.cn: 第一组收形近短词，第二组收表示清洁与除去的动词。

entries.definition: Broad from side to side.
entries.definitionCN: 宽的

entries.definition: A thin thread of metal.
entries.definitionCN: 电线；金属丝

entries.definition: A drink made from grapes.
entries.definitionCN: 葡萄酒

entries.definition: A blade that sweeps a windscreen.
entries.definitionCN: 雨刷

entries.definition: To remove dirt from something.
entries.definitionCN: 清洁

entries.definition: To move the hand firmly over a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 摩擦

entries.definition: To remove marks or data completely.
entries.definitionCN: 擦除；抹去

normalIntro.en: Wipe is a single short movement, so say it aloud while moving your hand across a table.
normalIntro.cn: wipe 就一个短动作，念它的时候顺手在桌上抹一下，就记住了。

normal.en: The w at the start is the shape of the cloth folding as you push it.
normal.cn: 开头的 w 像你推布时布面折起的形状。

normal.en: The silent e at the end keeps the i long, as in wide and white.
normal.cn: 末尾不发音的 e 让 i 保持长音，和 wide、white 一样。

normal.en: The past is wiped, not wipeed: drop the e before -ed.
normal.cn: 过去式是 wiped 而不是 wipeed：加 -ed 前要去掉 e。

normal.en: Add out and the cloth becomes a flood: wipe out.
normal.cn: 加上 out，布就变成了洪水：wipe out。

normal.en: A wiper is the same motion made by a machine on a windscreen.
normal.cn: wiper 是同样的动作，由机器在挡风玻璃上完成。

abstract.en: Water and crumbs pushed into a single line at the table edge.
abstract.cn: 水和碎屑被推到桌边，排成一条线。

abstract.en: A sleeve doing what a cloth should do.
abstract.cn: 袖子干了布该干的活。

abstract.en: A mark on a window that is there and then suddenly is not.
abstract.cn: 窗上的一道痕迹，在，然后忽然不在。

examples.en: Wipe your feet before you come in.
examples.cn: 进来之前把脚擦一擦。

examples.en: She wiped her eyes with the back of her hand.
examples.cn: 她用手背擦了擦眼睛。

examples.en: The storm wiped out the whole harvest in one night.
examples.cn: 一场风暴一夜之间毁掉了整季收成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 念 wipe 时手心朝下往外一抹，就是「擦」的动作。

root: 古英语 wipian（擦拭、抹净）→ 中古英语 wipen → wipe；同族有 wiper、wipeout、wet wipe。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins as one sweep of the hand, narrows to the thing carried away, then widens to total destruction, and finally names the movement itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从手的一道抹擦开始，收窄到被带走的东西，再扩展到彻底毁灭，最后命名这个动作本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wet cloth crossing a table in one sweep.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块湿布从桌子这头抹到那头。

branches.en: The cleaning branch: a table wiped twice before guests.
branches.cn: 清洁分支：客人来前擦了两遍的桌子。

branches.en: The removal branch: mud taken off boots at the door.
branches.cn: 除去分支：门口擦掉的靴上泥。

branches.en: The destruction branch: a bridge gone with the flood.
branches.cn: 毁灭分支：随洪水消失的桥。

branches.en: The noun branch: one quick pass with a dry cloth.
branches.cn: 名词分支：用干布快速抹一下。

branches.en: The vanishing branch: what is wiped leaves no mark behind.
branches.cn: 消失分支：被擦掉的不会留下痕迹。

intro.en: Wipe takes ordinary verb endings and builds compounds such as wipeout and the noun wiper.
intro.cn: wipe 能接普通动词词尾，也能构成 wipeout 与名词 wiper。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic and has no Latin ancestor; the Latin entry is a borrowed synonym.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根属于日耳曼语，没有拉丁语祖先；拉丁条目只是借入的同义词。

items.example: It is the plain verb and noun.

items.meaning: the one or the tool that wipes

items.example: The act turned into an object.

definition_zh: 霜；霜冻
definition_en: white ice crystals on cold surfaces, or freezing weather
core_image: 清晨的草叶上结着细细的白霜
scene: 清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。 A layer of frost covered the grass in the morning.
sceneCN: 这里 frost 是「霜」（第 1 个义项）；句意：清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。

derivatives.zh: 有霜的；冷淡的
除霜
糖霜

senses.title: White ice crystals
senses.definition: thin white ice that forms on cold surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 在寒冷表面形成的薄白冰晶
senses.example: A layer of frost covered the grass in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨的草地上覆着一层白霜。
senses.why: This is the basic weather sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的天气义项。

senses.title: Freezing weather
senses.definition: a period of weather cold enough to damage plants
senses.definitionCN: 冷到足以冻坏植物的天气时段
senses.example: An early frost ruined the young shoots.
senses.exampleCN: 一场早霜毁了嫩芽。
senses.why: The white crystals stand for the cold that makes them.
senses.whyCN: 白霜代指造成它的寒冷。

senses.title: Icing on a cake
senses.definition: a sweet coating on baked food
senses.definitionCN: 烘焙食品表面的甜涂层
senses.example: The cake was covered with white frosting.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋糕上覆着一层白糖霜。
senses.why: The white coating looks like frost on a cold surface.
senses.whyCN: 白色涂层看起来像冷面上的霜。

intro.en: Frost is an old Germanic word for frozen white ice.
intro.cn: frost 是古老的日耳曼语词，指白色的冰晶。

items.en: Forst meant frost.
items.cn: forst 意为霜。

items.en: The form became frost.
items.cn: 词形演变为 frost。

items.en: It named the white ice of cold mornings.
items.cn: 它用来指寒冷清晨的白冰。

items.en: It also means a damaging cold spell.
items.cn: 它也指造成损害的一轮寒潮。

items.en: It is used for sugar icing on cakes.
items.cn: 它也被用来指蛋糕上的糖霜。

note.en: Frost is compared with similar-looking words and words for cold forms.
note.cn: 把 frost 与形近词以及表示寒冷凝结物的词作比较。

abstract.en: What freezes overnight can melt by noon.

core.en: Cold made white on a surface.

branches.en: Grass wears a thin white coat.

branches.en: The crystals and the cold that made them share a name.

intro.en: Frost builds words for icy surfaces and cold manner.

latinIntro.en: Frost is Germanic, not Latin.

definition_zh: 热爱；崇拜；爱慕；喜爱（口语）；敬奉神；喜爱做；极喜欢；仰慕赞美
definition_en: to love and admire someone or something very much, or to worship a god with devotion
core_image: 烛光前低头合掌：把心里最高的位置留给所敬所爱之物
scene: 海边的老教堂里，烛光排成一行，信徒们低头合掌，空气里只有蜡香。 The pilgrims adored the wooden statue in silence.
sceneCN: 这里 adore 是「敬奉圣物」（第 5 个义项：以宗教礼节对圣像表达敬意）；句意为朝圣者默默地敬奉那尊木像。

senses.title: To love someone very much
senses.definition: to love someone very much, with warmth and delight rather than solemnity
senses.definitionCN: 非常爱某人，带着温暖与喜悦，而不是庄严肃穆
senses.example: She adores her grandchildren and spoils them shamelessly.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常疼爱孙辈，毫无顾忌地宠着他们。
senses.why: The core image is hands folded before a candle: the highest place in the heart is given away.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是在烛光前合掌：心里最高的位置被让了出去。

senses.title: To worship a god
senses.definition: to honour a god with religious worship and devotion
senses.definitionCN: 以宗教敬拜与虔诚敬奉神明
senses.example: The villagers still adore the old goddess of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们仍然崇拜那条河的老女神。
senses.why: The folded hands are now raised to a deity: love is directed upward and outward.
senses.whyCN: 合掌的手这时朝向神祇：爱被指向上方与外在。

senses.title: To feel romantic devotion
senses.definition: to feel deep romantic love and devotion toward someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人怀有深切的爱恋与倾慕
senses.example: He adored her from the first evening they met.
senses.exampleCN: 从相识的第一个晚上起，他就爱慕着她。
senses.why: The highest place is given to one person, and the feeling is both tender and a little worshipful.
senses.whyCN: 最高的位置被让给某一个人，这份情感既温柔，又带一点膜拜意味。

senses.title: To like something very much in speech
senses.definition: in everyday speech, to like a thing or place very much in a warm, informal way
senses.definitionCN: 在日常口语中，以温暖随意的方式非常喜欢某物或某地
senses.example: I adore that little café on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 我特别喜欢街角那家小咖啡馆。
senses.why: The solemn gesture relaxes into a smile: the same word now carries everyday pleasure.
senses.whyCN: 庄重的姿势放松成一个微笑：同一个词如今承载日常的愉悦。

senses.title: To reverence a sacred image
senses.definition: to show religious reverence to a sacred image, relic, or shrine with ritual acts
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式性的举动对圣像、圣物或圣所表达宗教敬意
senses.example: The pilgrims adored the wooden statue in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者默默地敬奉那尊木像。
senses.why: The hands are folded before an object rather than a person: devotion becomes a ritual.
senses.whyCN: 合掌的对象是一件物品而非一个人：虔诚变成了仪式。

senses.title: To enjoy doing something
senses.definition: in the pattern adore doing something, to enjoy an activity very much
senses.definitionCN: 用于 adore doing something 结构，表示非常喜欢某项活动
senses.example: She adores walking along the shore at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常喜欢黎明时沿着海岸散步。
senses.why: The thing loved is now an action: the heart gives its highest place to a way of spending time.
senses.whyCN: 所爱之物此时是一个动作：心把最高的位置让给一种度过时间的方式。

senses.title: To be extremely fond of something
senses.titleCN: 极喜欢（某种食物或嗜好）
senses.definition: to have a strong, settled fondness for a particular food, object, or pastime
senses.definitionCN: 对某种食物、物品或消遣怀有强烈而固定的喜爱
senses.example: He adores chocolate and keeps a bar in his desk drawer.
senses.exampleCN: 他极喜欢巧克力，抽屉里总放着一块。
senses.why: A small, repeated pleasure takes the place of the god: the word's warmth settles on a habit.
senses.whyCN: 一种细小而反复的愉悦取代了神的位置：这个词的温热落在一种习惯上。

senses.title: To admire and praise intensely
senses.definition: to admire someone intensely and speak of them with great praise
senses.definitionCN: 极其仰慕某人，并以高度的赞美谈论其人
senses.example: The crowd adored the young singer and would not let her leave.
senses.exampleCN: 人群极度仰慕这位年轻歌手，不让她离开。
senses.why: The upward gaze and the folded hands combine: admiration becomes something close to worship.
senses.whyCN: 仰望的目光与合掌的姿态叠在一起：钦佩变得近乎崇拜。

intro.en: Adore comes from Latin adorare, a verb of speaking to a god, and its oldest sense is prayer rather than affection.
intro.cn: adore 来自拉丁语 adorare，本是一个对神说话的动词，最古老的意思是祈祷，而不是爱意。

items.en: orare meant 'to speak, plead, pray'; it is also the source of orator and oration.
items.cn: orare 意为「说话、恳求、祈祷」，也是 orator 与 oration 的来源。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus orare gave adorare, 'to speak to, pray to, worship'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 orare 构成 adorare，意为「对……说话、向……祈祷、敬拜」。

items.en: The noun adoratio named worship and the act of praying to a deity.
items.cn: 名词 adoratio 表示敬拜以及对神祈祷的行为。

items.en: Old French adorer kept the religious sense, and English took the word from it in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语 adorer 保留了宗教义，英语在中世纪从它借入这个词。

items.en: The meaning widened from worship to deep love, and then to everyday fondness for things and activities.
items.cn: 词义从「敬拜」扩展到深切的爱，再扩展到对事物与活动的日常喜爱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same orare root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of love, worship, and esteem.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 orare 词根的一族词；近义组收表示爱、崇拜与敬重的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for deep love, worship, or reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇敬、热爱、爱慕」，是本词的名词形式。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning lovable or charming; much lighter than adore.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可爱的、讨人喜欢的」，语气比 adore 轻得多。

entries.definition: An adjective describing a look or person full of love and reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满爱意的、崇敬的」，用于描述目光或人。

entries.definition: A person who adores someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇拜者、爱慕者」。

entries.definition: A skilled public speaker; it comes from the same Latin verb 'to speak'.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演说家」，同出拉丁语中表示「说话」的动词。

entries.definition: To honour a god or person with devotion; the religious core of adore.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇拜、敬奉」，正对应 adore 的宗教核心义。

entries.definition: To feel deep affection for someone; broader and plainer than adore.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爱」，比 adore 更宽、更朴素。

entries.definition: To treasure and care for someone or something; gentler and less exalted.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「珍爱、珍惜」，更温柔，也没有那么高的崇敬意味。

entries.definition: To feel deep respect and awe; solemn and mainly about esteem.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇敬」，庄重，主要强调敬意。

entries.definition: To admire someone excessively as an idol; stronger and often critical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「把……当偶像崇拜」，程度更强，常带批评意味。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb 'to pray' and the family that grew from it.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语动词「祈祷」，以及由它长出的词族。

normal.en: orare means to speak and pray, so adore began as speaking to a god.
normal.cn: orare 意为「说话、祈祷」，所以 adore 最初是「对神说话」。

normal.en: Oration, orator and adore share the same speaking root.
normal.cn: oration、orator 与 adore 共享同一个「说话」词根。

normal.en: Adoration and adorer keep the ador- base; adorable adds -able and becomes much lighter.
normal.cn: adoration 与 adorer 保留 ador- 词基；adorable 加了 -able，语气轻得多。

normal.en: Adore doing something is the pattern for activities, as in adore walking at dawn.
normal.cn: adore doing something 是表达喜爱活动的结构，如 adore walking at dawn。

normal.en: I adore chocolate is everyday fondness, not religious worship.
normal.cn: I adore chocolate 是日常的喜爱，并非宗教崇拜。

abstract.en: Picture a candle, two folded hands, and a head lowered: the body gives the highest place away.
abstract.cn: 想象一支蜡烛、合起的双手、低下的头：身体把最高的位置让了出去。

abstract.en: The same gesture can be turned toward a god, a lover, a singer, or a bar of chocolate.
abstract.cn: 同一个姿态可以朝向神、爱人、歌手，或一块巧克力。

abstract.en: The lower the head, the higher the object: that is why adore slides so easily from worship into fondness.
abstract.cn: 头低得越低，对象就越高：这正是 adore 能从敬拜轻易滑向喜爱的原因。

examples.en: She adores her grandchildren and spoils them shamelessly.
examples.cn: 她非常疼爱孙辈，毫无顾忌地宠着他们。

examples.en: I adore walking along the shore at dawn.
examples.cn: 我非常喜欢黎明时沿着海岸散步。

examples.en: The villagers still adore the old goddess of the river.
examples.cn: 村民们仍然崇拜那条河的老女神。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的朵」——烛光前低头合掌，把心里最高的位置让给所敬所爱

root: 拉丁语 adorare「向……祈祷、敬拜」由 ad-「向」加 orare「说话、恳求、祈祷」构成；orare 也是 orator「演说家」与 oration「演说」的来源。英语经古法语 adorer 借入，词义由「敬拜」扩展到深切的爱，再扩展到日常喜爱。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lower the head before something: a person loved, a god worshipped, a lover adored, a café liked, a relic revered, an activity enjoyed, a food craved, and a star admired.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在某物面前低下头：所爱的人、所崇拜的神、所爱慕的人、所喜欢的咖啡馆、所敬奉的圣物、所喜爱的活动、所贪恋的食物、所仰慕的明星。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands are folded before a candle, and the highest place in the heart is given away.
core.cn: 核心意象：在烛光前合掌，心里最高的位置被让了出去。

branches.en: THE BELOVED: a grandchild or a lover receives the highest place, warm and a little worshipful.
branches.cn: 所爱者线：孙辈或爱人得到最高的位置，既温暖又带一点膜拜。

branches.en: THE SACRED: a god or a relic is honoured with prayer and ritual.
branches.cn: 神圣线：神明或圣物以祈祷与仪式受到敬奉。

branches.en: THE EVERYDAY: a café or a bar of chocolate takes the same warm place in smaller form.
branches.cn: 日常线：咖啡馆或一块巧克力，以更小的形式占据同样温热的位置。

branches.en: THE ACTIVITY: an action one loves to do is given the place of honour.
branches.cn: 活动线：一件爱做的事被让到尊位。

branches.en: THE STAR: admiration for a person grows until it almost becomes worship.
branches.cn: 明星线：对某人的钦佩不断增长，几乎变成崇拜。

intro.en: Adore is built from a Latin prefix and a verb of prayer; English adds the familiar noun, adjective and adverb endings.
intro.cn: adore 由拉丁语前缀与表示「祈祷」的动词构成，英语再添加常见的名词、形容词与副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: orare, adorare and adoratio are recorded Latin words; orator shares the same speaking root.
latinIntro.cn: orare、adorare、adoratio 都是有记录的拉丁词，orator 共享同一个「说话」词根。

items.exampleCN: 它把 orare 变成 adorare。

items.example: The verb is the speaking root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是这一词族的「说话」词根。

items.example: It is the direct source of adore.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adore 的直接来源。

items.example: It is the Latin shape behind adoration.
items.exampleCN: 它是 adoration 背后的拉丁语形态。

definition_zh: 面具；面罩；口罩；掩饰；伪装；遮住；掩盖
definition_en: a covering worn over the face for disguise, performance or protection, a pad worn over the nose and mouth against infection, a false appearance that hides feelings, or to cover and conceal something
core_image: 一只手把一张薄薄的面具举到脸前，镜中人立刻换上了另一副表情
scene: 剧场后台的镜子前，演员把一张纸浆面具举到脸前，试着调整角度。 Behind the curtain a dozen dancers were adjusting masks of painted silk.
sceneCN: 这里 mask 是「面具」（第 1 个义项：罩在脸上用来伪装或表演的覆盖物）；句意为幕布后面，十来个舞者正在调整绘着花纹的丝质面具。图中可辨识物件：后台镜子、纸浆面具、幕布、丝质面具。

pos.zh: 面具；面罩；口罩；掩饰；伪装

derivatives.zh: 由 mask 加 -ed 构成，义为「戴面具的；蒙面的」
由 mask 加 -ing 构成，义为「遮盖；掩蔽」
由表示相反动作的前缀 un- 加 mask 构成，义为「揭下面具；揭露真面目」
经法语 mascarade 借入，与 mask 同出意大利语 maschera 一族，义为「假面舞会；伪装」

senses.title: A covering worn over the face
senses.definition: an object worn over the face to hide it, to frighten, or to protect it
senses.definitionCN: 罩在脸上用来遮住面孔、吓人或保护面孔的物件
senses.example: The actor held a paper mask up to the mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 演员把一张纸面具举到镜子前。
senses.why: The word reached English from the theatre, where a mask changes who the wearer appears to be, so the covering and the new face arrive in one object.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是从剧场进入英语的，在那里一张面具会改变戴者看起来是谁；遮盖与换脸因此是同一件东西的两面。

senses.title: A pad worn over the nose and mouth against infection
senses.definition: a piece of cloth or paper worn over the nose and mouth to filter air and reduce the spread of germs
senses.definitionCN: 罩在口鼻上、用来过滤空气并减少病菌传播的布片或纸片
senses.example: Every nurse in the ward wore a fresh mask for each shift.
senses.exampleCN: 病房里每位护士每班都换一只新口罩。
senses.why: Protection is the other half of the theatre sense: the same covering that hides a face can also stand between a face and what floats in the air.
senses.whyCN: 保护是剧场那层意思的另一半：同一张遮盖物既能把脸藏起来，也能把脸与空气里飘着的东西隔开。

senses.title: A false appearance that hides what a person feels
senses.definition: a way of behaving that hides true feelings or intentions from other people
senses.definitionCN: 一种把真实情绪或意图挡在别人视线之外的表现方式
senses.example: His cheerful mask slipped the moment the door closed.
senses.exampleCN: 门一关上，他那副快活的面具就掉了。
senses.why: If a mask can hand you another face, then a manner put on for other people is a mask in the same sense, and the word moves from pasteboard to behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 既然一张面具能给你换上另一张脸，那么为别人摆出的姿态就是同一意义上的面具，词义便从纸板走到了举止。

senses.title: To cover the face with a mask
senses.definition: to put a mask on someone or on your own face, or to cover a face in a picture
senses.definitionCN: 给某人或自己戴上面具，或在图像里把脸部遮住
senses.example: The dancers masked themselves before the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 幕布升起前，舞者们给自己戴上了面具。
senses.why: Once the noun names the object, the verb is simply the act of putting it on, and English routinely turns a covering into the gesture that applies it.
senses.whyCN: 名词一旦指那件东西，动词就只是把它戴上去的动作；英语常把一件遮盖物直接变成施加它的那个手势。

senses.title: To hide or keep something from being noticed
senses.definition: to conceal a feeling, a sound, a taste or a fact so that other people do not notice it
senses.definitionCN: 把情绪、声音、味道或事实藏起来，让别人察觉不到
senses.example: The engine's hum masked the noise of the door opening.
senses.exampleCN: 引擎的嗡鸣盖住了门被推开的声音。
senses.why: Anything laid over a surface hides what is under it, so the word for a face covering extends to smells, sounds and facts that something else has covered.
senses.whyCN: 凡是铺在表面上的东西都会遮住下面的事物，于是「遮脸之物」这个词也推到被别的东西盖住的气味、声音与事实。

intro.en: Mask is a word of uncertain origin that came to English through French and Italian theatre, and even its earliest recorded Latin form has no settled source.
intro.cn: mask 是一个来源不确定的词，经法语与意大利语剧场传入英语，连它有记录的最早拉丁形式也没有定论。

items.en: The earliest documented link is Medieval Latin masca, a word for a mask or a terrifying spectre; its own origin is uncertain and may lie outside Latin altogether.
items.cn: 有记录的最早环节是中古拉丁语 masca，指面具或骇人的幽灵；它本身的来源不确定，甚至可能根本不在拉丁语之内。

items.en: Italian maschera named the mask worn in street theatre and carnival, and the word travelled with touring performers.
items.cn: 意大利语 maschera 指街头戏剧与狂欢节上戴的面具，这个词随巡回演出的艺人一起流传。

items.en: French took it as masque, meaning both the mask itself and the masked entertainment staged at court.
items.cn: 法语借作 masque，既指面具本身，也指宫廷里演的假面娱乐。

items.en: Middle English maske named a covering for the face and a disguise, and the spelling settled as mask in modern English.
items.cn: 中古英语 maske 指遮脸之物与伪装，现代英语里拼写固定为 mask。

items.en: Modern English keeps the theatre mask, adds the protective mask of medicine and industry, and uses the verb for hiding feelings, sounds and facts.
items.cn: 现代英语保留戏剧面具，又加上医学与工业上的防护面罩，并用动词表示掩盖情绪、声音与事实。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derivatives and the theatrical relatives of the word; the near group gathers other coverings and verbs of hiding.
note.cn: 形近组收这个词的派生词与戏剧上的同族词；近义组收其他遮盖物以及表示隐藏的动词。

entries.definition: Wearing a mask, or hidden from view, formed from mask with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 戴着面具的；被遮住看不见的；由 mask 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: To remove someone's mask, or to reveal what they really are.
entries.definitionCN: 揭下某人的面具；揭露其真面目；由 un- 加 mask 构成。

entries.definition: A party where people wear masks and costumes, or a pretence kept up in public.
entries.definitionCN: 人们戴面具、穿戏服的舞会；也指在众人面前维持的伪装；与 mask 同出意大利语 maschera 一族。

entries.definition: A courtly entertainment with music, dancing and masks, popular in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
entries.definitionCN: 十六、十七世纪流行的宫廷娱乐，含音乐、舞蹈与面具；与 mask 同出法语 masque。

entries.definition: A change of appearance or manner meant to hide who you are.
entries.definitionCN: 为隐藏身份而改变外貌或举止；伪装。

entries.definition: A piece of thin cloth worn over the face or head, or anything that hides something.
entries.definitionCN: 罩在脸上或头上的薄布；也指任何遮蔽物。

entries.definition: To place something over another thing so that it cannot be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物盖在另一物上，使它看不见。

entries.definition: To hide something or keep it from being known.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物藏起来，或使它不为人知。

normalIntro.en: The word came in with masked players rather than with doctors, and its family keeps returning to the changed face, the barrier and the thing hidden underneath.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是随戴面具的演员而不是医生进入英语的，它的同族词反复回到换过的脸、那道屏障，以及被遮在下面的东西。

normal.en: The record starts with Medieval Latin masca, a mask or a spectre, and even that word's origin is uncertain.
normal.cn: 记录从中古拉丁语 masca 开始，指面具或幽灵，而连这个词的来源都不确定。

normal.en: Italian maschera belonged to carnival and street theatre, so the English word arrived with performers rather than with physicians.
normal.cn: 意大利语 maschera 属于狂欢节与街头戏剧，所以这个词是随演员而不是随医生来到英语的。

normal.en: Unmask is simply un- plus mask, the gesture of taking the covering off, and therefore of showing the truth.
normal.cn: unmask 就是 un- 加 mask，即把遮盖物取下来的动作，因此也就是把真相露出来。

normal.en: The medical mask keeps the object and changes the purpose, from hiding a face to shielding one.
normal.cn: 医用口罩留着同一件东西，却换了目的，从把脸藏起来变成把脸护起来。

normal.en: The verb mask works on sounds and facts as easily as on faces, because anything laid over a surface hides what lies beneath.
normal.cn: 动词 mask 用在声音与事实上和用在脸上一样顺手，因为任何铺在表面上的东西都会遮住下面的内容。

abstract.en: A second face held in one hand: the word never quite separates covering from pretending.
abstract.cn: 一张被单手举着的第二张脸：这个词始终没能把遮盖与假装彻底分开。

abstract.en: The same paper square can hide a robber or protect a nurse, and the word does not care which.
abstract.cn: 同一方纸片既能遮住强盗，也能护住护士，而这个词并不在意是哪一种。

abstract.en: What masks a sound also masks a fact, and a theatre trick becomes an ordinary verb.
abstract.cn: 能盖住声音的东西也能盖住事实，一个舞台把戏就这样变成了寻常动词。

examples.en: The actor held a paper mask up to the mirror.
examples.cn: 演员把一张纸面具举到镜子前。

examples.en: Every nurse in the ward wore a fresh mask for each shift.
examples.cn: 病房里每位护士每班都换一只新口罩。

examples.en: The engine's hum masked the noise of the door opening.
examples.cn: 引擎的嗡鸣盖住了门被推开的声音。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马斯克」——马斯克戴上口罩和面具，走进会场谁也认不出他；记住 mask 是面具、口罩，也是掩盖。

root: 中古拉丁语 masca（面具、幽灵）来源不确定，一般认为经意大利语 maschera 与法语 masque 进入英语，也可能与阿拉伯语或意大利地方语有关，尚无定论。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a covering held in front of the face; the senses then divide into performance, protection, a front put on for others, the act of putting it on, and anything that hides what lies beneath.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是举在脸前的一件遮盖物；义项由此分成表演、防护、为别人摆出的门面、戴上它的动作，以及任何遮住下方事物的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one hand raising a thin mask to the face, and the reflection in the mirror instantly wearing another expression.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一张薄面具举到脸前，镜中人立刻换上了另一副表情。

branches.en: a paper mask lifted to a backstage mirror
branches.cn: 后台镜子前举起的一张纸面具

branches.en: nurses changing masks between shifts
branches.cn: 护士们在班次之间换口罩

branches.en: a cheerful face dropping at a closing door
branches.cn: 门一关上就垮掉的快活面孔

branches.en: dancers masking themselves before the curtain
branches.cn: 幕布升起前舞者给自己戴上面具

branches.en: an engine hum covering the sound of a door
branches.cn: 引擎嗡鸣盖住开门声

intro.en: An uncertain Medieval Latin noun, its Italian and French theatrical descendants, the English word and three English affixes carry mask from a stage prop to a medical pad and an ordinary verb of hiding.
intro.cn: 一个来源不确定的中古拉丁名词、它在意大利语与法语里的戏剧后代、英语本词，再加三个英语词缀，把 mask 从舞台道具带到医用垫片，再带到寻常的隐藏动词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable classical Latin cognate is recorded; the earliest documented form is Medieval Latin masca, itself of uncertain origin, so no Latin relatives are listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的古典拉丁同族词记录；有记录的最早形式是中古拉丁语 masca，其来源本身不确定，所以下面不列拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: to remove a mask, to expose

definition_zh: 奖章；勋章；奖牌；纪念章
definition_en: a piece of metal, often round and worn on a ribbon, given to honour a person or to mark a victory or an event
core_image: 一枚挂在深红色绸带上的圆形金属牌，正面刻着花纹与年份
scene: 颁奖台上，红布铺就的长桌摆着一只打开的丝绒盒，里面静静躺着刚铸好的圆牌。 She wore the medal only on the day her father came home.
sceneCN: 这里是「奖章、勋章」（第 1 个义项：授予荣誉的金属牌）；句意为她只在父亲回家的那天才戴上那枚奖章。图中可辨识物件：丝绒盒、绸带、颁奖长桌。

derivatives.zh: 由 medal 加 -ist 构成，义为「奖牌获得者」，英式拼写
medallist 的美式拼写，义为「奖牌获得者」
由 medal 加 -ic 构成，义为「奖章的；像奖章一样的」
与 medal 同源，经法语指「大圆牌；圆形饰物」

senses.title: A metal piece given as an honour
senses.definition: a metal disc, often with a ribbon, given to someone to honour courage, service or achievement
senses.definitionCN: 常配绸带的金属圆牌，授予某人以表彰其勇气、贡献或成就
senses.example: He was given a medal for thirty years of service.
senses.exampleCN: 他因服务三十年而获授一枚奖章。
senses.why: The earliest medals were stamped pieces of metal, valued because the metal itself was precious and the stamp spoke for the giver.
senses.whyCN: 最早的奖章是把金属压印成牌，珍贵既在金属本身，也在印记代表着授予者的话。

senses.title: A prize in a competition
senses.definition: one of the metal discs, gold, silver or bronze, awarded to the top finishers in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 比赛中颁给名次靠前者的一枚金属牌，分金、银、铜
senses.example: She took the silver medal in the relay.
senses.exampleCN: 她在接力赛中拿到银牌。
senses.why: Once sport needed a visible ranking, the same stamped disc became a ladder of colours, with gold at the top.
senses.whyCN: 当体育比赛需要看得见的排名，同一枚压印圆牌就变成一条按颜色排列的梯子，金色在最上。

senses.title: A commemorative piece
senses.definition: a similar metal piece made to remember a person, a place or an event rather than to reward anyone
senses.definitionCN: 为纪念某个人、某个地方或某件事而制作的同类金属牌，不以奖励为目的
senses.example: The museum sells a medal marking the opening of the new hall.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆出售一种纪念新展厅开幕的纪念章。
senses.why: If a stamped disc can honour a person, it can also simply mark a date, so the word split off a branch with no prize attached.
senses.whyCN: 既然压印的圆牌能表彰一个人，也就能单纯标记一个日子，于是分出一支不带奖赏意味的用法。

intro.en: Medal goes back to Latin metallum, the word for metal, and reached English through Italian and French after first naming small coins and stamped pieces.
intro.cn: medal 可追溯到拉丁语 metallum（金属），先指小钱币与压印的金属块，再经意大利语与法语进入英语。

items.en: Metallum meant metal, the material from which early coins and medals were struck.
items.cn: metallum 意为金属，早期钱币与奖章都由这种材料压成。

items.en: Medieval Latin used medalia for a small coin or a metal piece of half a denarius.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 medalia 指小钱币，或值半个第纳里的金属块。

items.en: Italian medaglia named a coin and then a portrait piece worn as an ornament or honour.
items.cn: 意大利语 medaglia 先指钱币，后指可佩戴的肖像牌，用作饰物或荣誉。

items.en: French médaille carried the honour sense into descriptions of commemorative and military pieces.
items.cn: 法语 médaille 把荣誉的含义带入对纪念牌与军功章的描述。

items.en: English medal covers awards, sporting prizes and souvenirs, while metal kept the plain material sense.
items.cn: 英语 medal 涵盖奖章、比赛奖牌与纪念品，而 metal 保留单纯的材料义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the metal-and-coin family plus two words that only resemble the spelling; the near-meaning group collects objects of recognition.
note.cn: 形近组收金属与钱币词族，另加两个只是拼写相像的词；近义组收表示表彰与荣誉的物品。

entries.definition: A large round metal piece worn as a decoration or keepsake.
entries.definitionCN: 作为饰物或信物佩戴的大圆金属牌。

entries.definition: A hard material such as iron or gold, from which medals are made.
entries.definitionCN: 铁、金之类坚硬的材料，奖章正由它制成。

entries.definition: Only the spelling is close; this verb means to interfere, with no link to metal or medals.
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近，这个词意为「干涉」，与金属或奖章没有词源关系。

entries.definition: Only the shape of the word is similar; it means a small copy or an example, from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 只是词形相似，意为「模型；范例」，词源不同。

entries.definition: A prize or honour given for an achievement.
entries.definitionCN: 因成就而颁发的奖品或荣誉。

entries.definition: An object, often a cup or figure, given as a prize for a win.
entries.definitionCN: 作为胜利奖品颁发的物品，常为奖杯或雕像。

entries.definition: A small piece of metal or cloth worn to show rank, membership or identity.
entries.definitionCN: 佩戴以显示级别、身份或成员资格的小金属牌或布章。

entries.definition: An honour such as a medal or title, or the act of adorning something.
entries.definitionCN: 勋章、称号之类的荣誉；也指装饰行为。

normalIntro.en: The word grows out of the word for metal, and the family keeps the idea of a stamped disc that carries value or honour.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从表示金属的词长出来，同族词一直保留「压印的圆牌承载价值或荣誉」这一想法。

normal.en: Metal is the base: a medal is a piece of metal stamped with meaning.
normal.cn: metal 是底子：奖章就是一块被压印出意义的金属。

normal.en: Medallion is a large medal-like piece, from the same root and the same shape.
normal.cn: medallion 是大号的奖章式圆牌，同根也同形。

normal.en: The three colours of Olympic medals make the word a visible ranking.
normal.cn: 奥运奖牌的三色，让这个词成了一种看得见的排名。

normal.en: A medal for service rewards time; a medal in sport rewards speed, but the object is the same.
normal.cn: 服务奖章奖励的是年头，体育奖牌奖励的是速度，但物件是同一个。

normal.en: The -ist ending turns medal into medallist, the person who takes one home.
normal.cn: 加 -ist 就把 medal 变成 medallist，即把奖牌带回家的人。

abstract.en: A medal is metal turned into memory, a cheap material made precious by the words said when it is pinned on.
abstract.cn: 奖章是把金属变成记忆：便宜的材料，因别上时说的那几句话而变得珍贵。

abstract.en: The same disc can honour a life or rank a race, which shows how one object can carry two kinds of value.
abstract.cn: 同一枚圆牌既能表彰一生，也能给一场比赛排名，这说明一个物件可以承载两种价值。

abstract.en: A medal is worn on the body, so the honour is kept close to the heart rather than filed away.
abstract.cn: 奖章戴在身上，所以荣誉是贴近心口保存的，而不是归档收起来的。

examples.en: He kept his grandfather's medal in a wooden box.
examples.cn: 他把祖父的奖章收在一只木盒里。

examples.en: The team won three medals at the regional games.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在地区运动会上赢了三枚奖牌。

examples.en: Every medal on the wall marks a year of hard training.
examples.cn: 墙上的每一枚奖牌都标记着一年的刻苦训练。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「美的」——比赛的奖章做得很美；记住 medal 是奖章。

root: 拉丁语 metallum（金属）经中世纪拉丁语 medalia、意大利语 medaglia 与法语 médaille 进入英语；同族词与金属、钱币、圆牌有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a stamped metal disc; the senses then split by purpose into an honour, a sporting prize and a souvenir of memory.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一枚压印的金属圆牌；义项按用途分出荣誉、比赛奖牌与纪念信物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round metal disc hanging from a dark red ribbon, its face stamped with a pattern and a year.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚挂在深红绸带上的圆形金属牌，正面压印着花纹与年份。

branches.en: a ribbon pinned to a uniform after a long career
branches.cn: 漫长职业生涯后别在制服上的绸带

branches.en: three discs gleaming on a stand at a race
branches.cn: 赛场上领奖台上闪光的三枚圆牌

branches.en: a crowd counting the colours on an athlete's chest
branches.cn: 人群数着运动员胸前的颜色

branches.en: a velvet box sold beside a museum door
branches.cn: 博物馆门口出售的丝绒盒

branches.en: a wall of tiny discs each tied to one name
branches.cn: 一面挂满小圆牌、每枚对应一个名字的墙

intro.en: The word is carried by Latin metal, a medieval coin term, an Italian ornamental piece, the French form and two English endings.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语「金属」、中世纪钱币词、意大利语饰牌、法语形式与两个英语词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 积极地；主动地；活跃地
definition_en: in a way that shows effort and direct participation
core_image: 讨论桌旁，一只手总是第一个举起来
scene: 每次课堂讨论，她都积极发言。 She actively participates in every class discussion.
sceneCN: 这里的 actively 是「积极地」（第 1 个义项：主动参与）；句意是她在每次课堂讨论中都积极发言。

derivatives.zh: 由副词去后缀还原为形容词，义为「积极的；活跃的」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「活动」
由词干加动词后缀构成，义为「激活」

senses.title: With direct personal effort
senses.definition: by taking part and putting in effort rather than staying passive
senses.definitionCN: 以参与并出力的方式，而不是被动旁观
senses.example: The students actively shaped the new rules.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们积极参与制定了新规则。
senses.why: The adverb carries the adjective's idea of being able to act and applies it to the manner of doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词带着形容词「能行动」的意思，落在做事的方式上。

senses.title: With continuing energy
senses.definition: in a way that keeps operating or growing strongly
senses.definitionCN: 以持续运转或强劲增长的方式
senses.example: The company is actively recruiting engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 公司正在积极招聘工程师。
senses.why: Effort can also be steady rather than sudden, so the adverb describes an ongoing push rather than a single step.
senses.whyCN: 努力也可以是持续而非一时的，于是这个副词描述的是不断推进，而不是单独一步。

intro.en: The adverb is active plus the manner ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个副词就是 active 加方式词尾 -ly。

items.en: agere meant to drive or to do.
items.cn: agere 意为驱动或做。

items.en: activus meant able to act.
items.cn: activus 意为能行动的。

items.en: active entered English as an adjective.
items.cn: active 作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: the ending -ly produced the adverb actively.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 造出副词 actively。

items.en: it now modifies verbs of joining, seeking and supporting.
items.cn: 如今它修饰参与、寻求与支持一类动词。

note.en: The first group is the active family; the second is other adverbs of energetic action.
note.cn: 第一组是 active 词族；第二组是别的表示积极行动的副词。

entries.definition: taking part
entries.definitionCN: 积极的

entries.definition: a thing people do
entries.definitionCN: 活动

entries.definition: to set in motion
entries.definitionCN: 激活

entries.definition: the act of doing
entries.definitionCN: 行动

entries.definition: with force and liveliness
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛地

entries.definition: with strong desire
entries.definitionCN: 热切地

entries.definition: in a constructive way
entries.definitionCN: 正面地

entries.definition: without taking action
entries.definitionCN: 被动地

normalIntro.en: The adverb is the adjective active with -ly attached.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是形容词 active 加 -ly。

normal.en: active plus -ly tells how someone takes part.
normal.cn: active 加 -ly，说明一个人如何参与。

normal.en: actively involved is the most frequent pairing.
normal.cn: actively involved 是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: passively is the direct opposite in form and meaning.
normal.cn: passively 在形式与意思上都是直接反义。

normal.en: the comparative uses more, not -lier.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more，而不是加 -lier。

normal.en: companies actively recruit when they are growing.
normal.cn: 公司在扩张时会积极地招人。

abstract.en: See the same hand rise first in every discussion.
abstract.cn: 想象每次讨论都是同一只手先举起来。

abstract.en: Picture a shop with its door open before sunrise.
abstract.cn: 想象一家店在日出前就开了门。

abstract.en: Think of a runner leaning forward into the hill.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者身体前倾，迎向坡道。

examples.en: Parents should actively listen to their children.
examples.cn: 父母应当积极地倾听孩子。

examples.en: The group actively campaigns for cleaner air.
examples.cn: 这个团体积极推动更清洁的空气。

examples.en: She was actively involved in the rescue.
examples.cn: 她积极参与了救援。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿克提夫利」——阿克提着一股劲头，凡事都抢在前头利落地做。

root: 由 active（拉丁语 activus，能行动的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；词根 agere 意为驱动、做，表示以主动、持续出力的方式。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb marks both a single act of joining in and a steady push over time.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词既标记一次主动加入，也标记长期持续的推进。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that moves before being asked.
core.cn: 核心意象：不用人叫就先动起来的手。

branches.en: joining a discussion without being called
branches.cn: 不用点名就加入讨论

branches.en: a company hiring through the season
branches.cn: 整个季度都在招人的公司

branches.en: parents listening before they advise
branches.cn: 先倾听再建议的父母

branches.en: a campaign that keeps pushing
branches.cn: 持续推进的运动

branches.en: one choice repeated until it becomes a habit
branches.cn: 一次选择重复到成为习惯

intro.en: The adjective stem plus the manner ending forms the adverb.
intro.cn: 形容词词干加方式词尾，构成这个副词。

latinIntro.en: The root agere also gives agent and agenda.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 agere 也给出 agent 与 agenda。

definition_zh: 闪电；一次放电；雷击；球状闪电；闪电般的；突如其来的打击
definition_en: the bright flash of atmospheric electricity, or a single discharge of it, often striking the ground
core_image: 漆黑云层里骤然裂开一道折线状的白光，瞬间照亮整片原野又立刻消失
scene: 雷雨夜里，一道白光把路旁的老橡树从中间劈开。 A single lightning strike split the old oak beside the road.
sceneCN: 这里指「大气放电产生的闪电，一次击中地面」（第 1 个义项：云地之间的一次放电通道）；句意为一次雷击把路旁的老橡树劈成两半。图中可辨识物件：折线状的电光、被劈裂的树干、雨幕、被照亮的路面；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The flash of atmospheric electricity
senses.definition: the bright flash produced when electrical charge in a cloud discharges through the air
senses.definitionCN: 云中电荷通过空气放电时产生的明亮闪光
senses.example: A single lightning strike split the old oak beside the road.
senses.exampleCN: 一次雷击把路旁的老橡树劈成两半。
senses.why: The noun names the visible event, the flash, rather than the invisible charge that causes it.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名的是可见的事件——那道闪光，而不是造成它的不可见电荷。

senses.title: A single discharge stroke
senses.definition: one return stroke of a discharge, which may repeat several times within a single flash
senses.definitionCN: 一次放电的回击，同一道闪光内可重复数次
senses.example: Instruments recorded four strokes inside one lightning flash.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器记录到一道闪电内包含四次回击。
senses.why: Physics needs to separate the flash we see from the strokes that compose it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学需要把肉眼所见的闪光与构成它的回击分开。

senses.title: A strike that hits something
senses.definition: a discharge that reaches the ground or an object and damages it
senses.definitionCN: 到达地面或某物体并造成损害的放电
senses.example: Lightning struck the church tower twice that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那年夏天，雷击了教堂塔楼两次。
senses.why: Once the flash touches something, the event becomes an impact with consequences.
senses.whyCN: 当闪光触到某物，事件就变成了一次有后果的撞击。

senses.title: Ball lightning
senses.definition: a rare glowing sphere reported to float for seconds after a strike
senses.definitionCN: 雷击后据报可漂浮数秒的罕见发光球体
senses.example: Witnesses described ball lightning drifting through the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 目击者描述球状闪电飘过厨房。
senses.why: The subtype keeps the base word and adds a shape, because the phenomenon is still classed as a discharge.
senses.whyCN: 这一下位类型保留原词并加上形状，因为该现象仍被归入放电。

senses.title: Extremely fast, as an attributive
senses.titleCN: 闪电般极快的（定语用法）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean extremely quick, as in lightning speed or a lightning response
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前表示极快，如闪电般的速度或反应
senses.example: The agency mounted a lightning response to the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对疫情作出了闪电般的响应。
senses.why: Speed is read off the flash: the light appears and is gone before the eye can follow.
senses.whyCN: 速度是从闪光读出来的：光出现又消失，眼睛来不及跟上。

senses.title: A very brief visit or event
senses.titleCN: 极短暂的一次到访或事件
senses.definition: a short, intense visit or event that begins and ends almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 开始与结束几乎同时发生的短暂而强烈的到访或事件
senses.example: The minister made a lightning visit to the flooded town.
senses.exampleCN: 部长对受淹城镇做了一次闪电式访问。
senses.why: The metaphor borrows duration, not electricity: what matters is that there is almost no interval.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻借用的是时长而非电：要点在于几乎没有间隔。

senses.title: A sudden shock of insight or disaster
senses.titleCN: 突如其来的灵感或打击
senses.definition: a sudden, illuminating idea or a sudden destructive event likened to a flash
senses.definitionCN: 被比作闪光的突然顿悟，或突然的破坏性事件
senses.example: The solution came to her like lightning in the middle of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 答案在半夜像闪电一样击中了她。
senses.why: Both insight and catastrophe arrive without warning, which is the single feature the metaphor keeps.
senses.whyCN: 顿悟与灾祸都不打招呼就到，这正是该比喻保留的唯一特征。

senses.title: Sheet lightning without audible thunder
senses.titleCN: 只现光而听不到雷的片状闪电
senses.definition: a diffuse flash seen without a distinct channel, usually from a distant storm whose thunder is unheard
senses.definitionCN: 看不到清晰通道的弥散闪光，通常来自雷声已不可闻的远处风暴
senses.example: Heat lightning flickered along the southern horizon all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 整个傍晚，南边地平线上闪着无声的片状闪电。
senses.why: When the stroke is too far away for sound, only the illuminated cloud sheet remains visible.
senses.whyCN: 当放电太远、声音传不到时，剩下的只有被照亮的云幕。

intro.en: Lightning began as lightening, the verbal noun of lighten 'to flash', and lost its medial e in the modern spelling. The verb goes back to Old English lēoht 'light', a Germanic word whose Indo-European stock also produced Latin lux.
intro.cn: lightning 最初写作 lightening，是动词 lighten「发闪」的动名词，现代拼写中丢掉了中间的 e。该动词可溯至古英语 lēoht「光」，这一日耳曼词所属的印欧词干也产生了拉丁 lux。

items.en: Old English lēoht meant 'light, brightness' and also 'not heavy', a pair of senses still kept by the modern word light.
items.cn: 古英语 lēoht 既指「光、明亮」，也指「不重」，现代词 light 仍保留这两组意思。

items.en: In Middle English the flashing was called lightening, the -ing noun of the verb lighten 'to flash'; the modern spelling dropped the e.
items.cn: 中古英语把闪电现象称作 lightening，即动词 lighten「发闪」的 -ing 名词；现代拼写丢掉了那个 e。

items.en: German Leuchten 'to shine' and Dutch licht belong to the same Germanic stock, so the word is native rather than borrowed.
items.cn: 德语 Leuchten「发光」与荷兰语 licht 属同一日耳曼词干，因此该词是本族词而非借词。

items.en: Latin lux, lucis 'light' and lucere 'to shine' are distant cousins through Indo-European *leuk-, not ancestors of the English word.
items.cn: 拉丁 lux, lucis「光」与 lucere「发光」经印欧 *leuk- 与之远亲同源，并非英语词的祖先。

items.en: Only the weather sense survives in ordinary use; the verb lighten in the sense 'to flash' is now archaic.
items.cn: 日常使用中只剩天气义；动词 lighten 的「发闪」义现已古旧。

items.en: Source uncertain (spelling history): the loss of the medial e is usually explained by contraction in fast speech, but no single documented path is agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（拼写史）：中间 e 的脱落通常用快速语流中的缩合解释，但没有公认的单一文献路径。

note.en: Group one holds the words most often confused with lightning by spelling; group two holds names for the same flash or for its parts.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写最易与本词混淆的词；第二组是同一道闪光或其组成部分的名称。

entries.definition: To make lighter or less heavy, or to brighten; despite the shared letters it is not the modern noun for the flash.
entries.definitionCN: 使更轻或更亮；尽管字形相近，它并不是现代指闪电的名词。

entries.definition: The equipment or design of lights in a room or on a stage; it has nothing to do with weather.
entries.definitionCN: 房间或舞台的灯具与布光；与天气无关。

entries.definition: A metal rod that carries a strike safely to earth; the compound keeps the base word unchanged.
entries.definitionCN: 把雷击安全导入地面的金属杆；复合词保留原词形不变。

entries.definition: A shaft of lightning, or the act of striking; shorter and more concrete than the phenomenon itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一道闪电，或一次击中；比作为现象的闪电更短、更具体。

entries.definition: The instant of light, not the electrical process that lies behind it.
entries.definitionCN: 光出现的那一瞬，而非其背后的放电过程。

entries.definition: A lightning stroke imagined as a weapon, common in myth and older prose.
entries.definitionCN: 被想象成武器的雷击，多见于神话与旧体散文。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real source verb, the real cognates and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的来源动词、真实的同源词与真实的复合词。

normal.en: The word was once lightening, the -ing noun of the verb lighten 'to flash'.
normal.cn: 该词原本写作 lightening，即动词「发闪」的 -ing 名词。

normal.en: Latin lux and lucere are cousins through the same Indo-European stock, not ancestors.
normal.cn: 拉丁 lux 与 lucere 是同一印欧词干的远亲，而不是祖先。

normal.en: Compounds keep the base unchanged: lightning rod, lightning bolt, lightning strike.
normal.cn: 复合词保留原词形：避雷针、一道闪电、雷击。

normal.en: Resultative verb pattern: lightning struck the tower.
normal.cn: 结果动词模式：闪电击中了塔楼。

normal.en: The attributive use carries speed: lightning speed, a lightning response.
normal.cn: 定语用法承载速度义：闪电般的速度、闪电般的响应。

abstract.en: Picture a crack in the dark that lasts less than a heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗里裂开一道缝，持续时间不到一次心跳。

abstract.en: Picture a whole room lit for an instant, then darker than before.
abstract.cn: 想象整间屋子亮了一瞬，随后比先前更暗。

abstract.en: Picture an idea arriving with no warning and no sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头毫无预警、毫无声响地到来。

examples.en: Lightning lit the valley three times before the rain began.
examples.cn: 雨落下之前，闪电把山谷照亮了三次。

examples.en: The tower has been fitted with a lightning rod since the fire.
examples.cn: 那场火灾之后，塔楼装上了避雷针。

examples.en: News of the verdict spread at lightning speed.
examples.cn: 裁决的消息以闪电般的速度传开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「light（光）+ ning」——黑云里骤然亮起的光 → 闪电

root: 由动词 lighten「发闪」的 -ing 名词 lightening 缩合而来，可溯至古英语 lēoht「光」；与德语 Leuchten、荷兰语 licht 同源，并与拉丁 lux、lucere 经印欧 *leuk- 远亲同源。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the flash itself to a single stroke, its impact, a rare spherical form, then to speed, brevity, sudden shock and the distant sheet flash.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从闪光本身，走到单次回击、击中物体、罕见的球状形态，再走到速度、短暂、突然冲击与远处的片状闪光。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crack of white light that exists for an instant and then leaves the world darker.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只存在一瞬、随后让世界更暗的白光裂缝。

branches.en: EVENT AND UNIT: the visible flash and the single stroke are one discharge seen at two scales.
branches.cn: 事件与单位：可见的闪光与单次回击，是同一次放电在两种尺度上。

branches.en: WHERE IT LANDS: a strike gains consequences; a rare spherical form gains a shape.
branches.cn: 落在何处：击中某物便有了后果；罕见的球状形态则有了形状。

branches.en: BORROWED SPEED: the flash lends its instant to responses and visits.
branches.cn: 借来的速度：闪光把它的瞬间借给响应与到访。

branches.en: SUDDEN ARRIVAL: insight and disaster both come without warning.
branches.cn: 突然到来：顿悟与灾祸都不打招呼就到。

branches.en: FAR-OFF LIGHT: when sound cannot reach, only the lit cloud sheet is left.
branches.cn: 远方之光：声音到不了时，只剩被照亮的云幕。

intro.en: Lightning is a deverbal noun from a native verb, so its parts are English and Germanic rather than Latin.
intro.cn: lightning 是由本族动词派生的动名词，其成分属英语与日耳曼语，而非拉丁语。

latinIntro.en: Latin lux and lucere are cognate at the Indo-European level only; they are quoted here as cousins, not as sources.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 lux 与 lucere 仅在印欧语层面同源；此处把它们作为远亲引用，而非来源。

items.structure: light (Old English lēoht, noun and adjective)
items.example: The base supplies both brightness and lightness.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根同时提供「光」与「轻」两层意思。

items.example: The lightening was visible for miles.
items.exampleCN: 数英里外都能看见那次闪电。

items.meaning: a conductor that takes the strike
items.example: The rod ran down the side of the barn.
items.exampleCN: 避雷针沿着谷仓侧面接到地面。

items.example: A bolt scorched the fence post.
items.exampleCN: 一道闪电把栅栏柱烧焦了。

items.example: Lightning bugs rose from the wet grass.
The door was lightning-fast to open.
The reply came at lightning speed.
items.exampleCN: 回复以极快的速度到来。

definition_zh: 港口；海港；避难所；庇护
definition_en: a sheltered place where ships can stay, or to shelter something
core_image: 一群小船躲在防波堤后的静水里
scene: 渔船驶回了港口。 The fishing boats returned to the harbour.
sceneCN: 这里 harbour 是「港口」（第 1 个义项）；句意：渔船驶回了港口。

derivatives.zh: 停泊处
港务长

senses.title: Sheltered port
senses.definition: an area of water sheltered from the sea where ships can stay
senses.definitionCN: 避开外海风浪、可供船只停泊的水域
senses.example: The fishing boats returned to the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 渔船驶回了港口。
senses.why: This is the basic place sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的地点义项。

senses.title: Place of refuge
senses.definition: a place that gives safety from danger or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 使人免受危险或困扰的安全之处
senses.example: The library was a harbour from the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆是躲避喧闹的港湾。
senses.why: A port protects ships, so the word protects people too.
senses.whyCN: 港口护住船只，于是也用来护住人。

senses.title: Shelter someone
senses.definition: to give shelter to a person or animal
senses.definitionCN: 给人或动物提供藏身之处
senses.example: They harboured the stray dog.
senses.exampleCN: 他们收留了那只流浪狗。
senses.why: The noun of shelter became a verb.
senses.whyCN: 庇护的名词，转成了动词。

senses.title: Keep a feeling
senses.definition: to keep a thought or feeling secretly in the mind
senses.definitionCN: 在心里暗暗保留某种想法或情感
senses.example: He harboured doubts for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年心怀疑虑。
senses.why: The mind can be a harbour for thoughts.
senses.whyCN: 头脑也可以成为想法的港湾。

intro.en: Harbour comes from Old English herebeorg, an army shelter, later any refuge.
intro.cn: harbour 来自古英语 herebeorg（军队的营地），后来泛指避难所。

items.en: The root meant a shelter for an army.
items.cn: 该词根指军队的庇护所。

items.en: Herebeorg meant a lodging or camp.
items.cn: herebeorg 指住处或营地。

items.en: Harbour named a place of safety.
items.cn: harbour 指安全之处。

items.en: It became the usual word for a port.
items.cn: 它成为「港口」的常用词。

items.en: The verb named sheltering and holding ideas.
items.cn: 动词义指收留与心怀想法。

note.en: Harbour is compared with look-alike words and with words for ports and shelter.
note.cn: 把 harbour 与形近词以及表示港口和庇护的词作比较。

entries.definition: a sign of something coming
entries.definitionCN: 预兆

entries.definition: a person who cuts hair
entries.definitionCN: 理发师

entries.definition: the gathering of crops
entries.definitionCN: 收获

entries.definition: a town or place where ships load
entries.definitionCN: 港口

entries.definition: a place giving protection
entries.definitionCN: 庇护所

entries.definition: safety from danger
entries.definitionCN: 避难

normalIntro.en: A harbour holds ships, then holds people, then holds thoughts.
normalIntro.cn: 港口先容下船，再容下人，最后容下念头。

normal.en: The ship entered the harbour at dusk.
normal.cn: 船在黄昏时驶入港口。

normal.en: This bay is a natural harbour.
normal.cn: 这个海湾是天然良港。

normal.en: The church became a harbour for the homeless.
normal.cn: 教堂成了无家可归者的避难所。

normal.en: They harboured no anger.
normal.cn: 他们心里没有怨恨。

normal.en: She harbours a hope of returning.
normal.cn: 她怀着重返的希望。

abstract.en: Every ship needs a wall against the sea.
abstract.cn: 每条船，都需要一道挡海的墙。

abstract.en: A harbour says nothing and keeps everything.
abstract.cn: 港湾什么也不说，却容下一切。

abstract.en: The heart is the last harbour we build.
abstract.cn: 心，是我们建的最后一个港湾。

examples.en: The fishing boats returned to the harbour.
examples.cn: 渔船驶回了港口。

examples.en: The library was a harbour from the noise.
examples.cn: 图书馆是躲避喧闹的港湾。

examples.en: He harboured doubts for years.
examples.cn: 他多年心怀疑虑。

dict_mnemonic.text: harbour 是「港口」，也指「避难所」；作动词是「庇护、藏匿」，还可表示心里「怀有」想法或怨恨，harbour a grudge 是心怀怨恨。

root: 来自古英语 herebeorg（军队营地），源于日耳曼语；由庇护之所引申为港口与避难所，再引申为心里怀藏某种念头。

sensesIntro.en: Harbour is a sheltered port, a refuge, the act of sheltering, or a feeling kept inside.
sensesIntro.cn: harbour 是避风的港口、避难所、收留的动作，或藏在心里的情感。

core.en: Still water behind a breakwater.
core.cn: 防波堤后的静水。

branches.en: Boats line up behind a stone wall.
branches.cn: 小船排在石墙后。

branches.en: A tired walker finds a dry doorway.
branches.cn: 疲惫的行人找到一个干燥的门洞。

branches.en: A warm kitchen takes in a wet dog.
branches.cn: 温暖的厨房收留了一只湿透的狗。

branches.en: An old man keeps one quiet hope.
branches.cn: 老人守着一个安静的希望。

branches.en: A place and a mind can both give shelter.
branches.cn: 一个地方与一颗心，都能提供庇护。

intro.en: Harbour takes plural and verb endings and forms trade compounds.
intro.cn: harbour 加复数与动词词尾，并构成行业复合词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.meaning: an official in charge of a port
items.exampleCN: 港务长招手让我们进港。

items.example: The cove is a safe harbour.

definition_zh: 突然的；意外的；陡峭的；唐突的；生硬的
definition_en: sudden and unexpected, steep, or short and rude in manner
core_image: 一句话还没说完，声音就被硬生生折断
scene: 山路忽然断在一处塌方前，队伍不得不停住脚步。 The hike came to an abrupt stop when the trail collapsed.
sceneCN: 这里 abrupt 是「突然的、意外的」（第 1 个义项：事情毫无预兆地发生）；句意为小径塌方时，徒步突然中断了。

pos.zh: 形容词：突然的；意外的；陡峭的；唐突的；生硬的

derivatives.zh: 由 abrupt 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「突然地；唐突地」
由 abrupt 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「突然；唐突；陡峭」
由拉丁词干 abrupt- 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「突然分离、中断」，多用于医学

senses.title: Sudden and unexpected
senses.definition: happening suddenly and without warning
senses.definitionCN: 毫无预兆地突然发生
senses.example: The meeting came to an abrupt halt when the power failed.
senses.exampleCN: 停电时会议突然中止了。
senses.why: The Latin participle meant broken off; what is broken off has no warning and no smooth lead-in.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「被折断的」；被折断的东西没有预兆，也没有平缓的过渡。

senses.title: Ending a process short
senses.definition: ending a process, discussion, or activity before its natural finish
senses.definitionCN: 让过程、讨论或活动在自然结束之前中断
senses.example: The abrupt end of the talks surprised both delegations.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈的突然终止让两个代表团都很意外。
senses.why: A conversation is a continuous line; breaking it leaves the line cut in the middle.
senses.whyCN: 对话是一条连续的线；把它折断，线就停在中间。

senses.title: Steep, of a slope
senses.definition: rising or falling very steeply, with little horizontal distance
senses.definitionCN: 上升或下降非常陡，水平距离很短
senses.example: The path turned into an abrupt climb near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 接近山顶时，小路变成一段陡峭的爬升。
senses.why: A steep slope is a surface that breaks sharply upward instead of rising gradually.
senses.whyCN: 陡坡是一面陡然向上折断的表面，而不是缓缓升起的坡。

senses.title: Rude and offhand in manner
senses.definition: speaking or acting in a way that seems rude, cold, and unfriendly
senses.definitionCN: 说话或行事显得无礼、冷淡、不友好
senses.example: His abrupt reply made the room go quiet.
senses.exampleCN: 他唐突的回答让屋里安静了下来。
senses.why: Social smoothness is a gradual slope; a person who cuts the conversation short seems broken off too.
senses.whyCN: 社交上的圆滑是一道缓坡；把话头直接切断的人，也像被折断一样。

senses.title: Short and cold, of an answer
senses.definition: expressed in very few words, with little warmth or explanation
senses.definitionCN: 只用很少几个字表达，缺少温度与解释
senses.example: She gave an abrupt nod and left.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡地点了下头就走了。
senses.why: An answer stripped of explanation is a sentence with its ending cut off.
senses.whyCN: 抽掉解释的回答，就是把句子的结尾剪掉。

senses.title: Disjointed, of style
senses.definition: lacking smooth connections, of writing, speech, or narrative style
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏顺畅衔接，用于文字、言语或叙事风格
senses.example: The abrupt style of the report was hard to follow.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告生硬的文风让人难以跟上。
senses.why: Style is judged by its transitions; where transitions are missing, the text looks broken into pieces.
senses.whyCN: 文风看的是衔接；衔接缺失，文本就像被折成一段一段。

senses.title: Sharp, of a change in amount
senses.definition: sharp and large, of a change in amount, level, or direction
senses.definitionCN: 数量、水平或方向发生又急又大的变化
senses.example: There was an abrupt rise in temperature at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 正午气温急剧上升。
senses.why: A graph that jumps instead of sloping gently looks like a line snapped upward.
senses.whyCN: 曲线陡然跳起而不是平缓上升，就像一条被向上折断的线。

senses.title: Without transition, in a sequence
senses.definition: moving from one scene or topic to another with no transition
senses.definitionCN: 从一个场景或话题直接跳到另一个，没有过渡
senses.example: The film makes an abrupt jump from one scene to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片从一个场景突兀地跳到下一个。
senses.why: A sequence is expected to flow; a jump breaks the flow, which is the same broken-line picture again.
senses.whyCN: 序列本应顺畅流动；突然一跳打断了流动，仍是同一条被折断的线。

intro.en: Abrupt comes straight from a Latin participle meaning broken off, built on the verb for breaking.
intro.cn: abrupt 直接来自一个意为「被折断的」拉丁分词，其基础动词表示「折断」。

items.en: rumpere meant to break or burst; it also supplies rupture and erupt.
items.cn: rumpere 意为「折断、爆裂」，还给出 rupture 与 erupt。

items.en: ab-, 'away', plus rumpere gave abrumpere, 'to break off'.
items.cn: ab-「离开」加 rumpere 构成 abrumpere，意为「折断、断掉」。

items.en: The past participle abruptus meant broken off, steep, or hasty, and English took it as an adjective.
items.cn: 过去分词 abruptus 意为「被折断的、陡的、仓促的」，英语直接把它当作形容词借用。

items.en: English abrupt is recorded from the sixteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 abrupt 自十六世纪起有记录；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word extended from broken terrain and broken speech to abrupt changes on graphs and in narratives.
items.cn: 这个词从断裂的地形与断裂的言语，扩展到图表与叙事中的突变。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the rumpere family and its Latin relatives; the near-meaning group gathers words for suddenness, steepness, and bluntness.
note.cn: 形近组收 rumpere 词族及其拉丁同族；近义组收表示突然、陡峭与生硬的词。

entries.definition: Suddenly and without transition, or in a rude, short manner.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「突然地；唐突地」，由 abrupt 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being sudden, steep, or blunt.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然；陡峭；唐突」，由 abrupt 加 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: A sudden breaking off or separation, used especially in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「突然分离、中断」，多用于医学，由拉丁词干加 -ion 构成。

entries.definition: To burst out, of a volcano or a sudden emotion, from the same Latin rumpere.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「爆发、喷发」，与 abrupt 同出拉丁语 rumpere「折断、爆裂」。

entries.definition: A break or burst, of a pipe, a relationship, or tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词，义为「破裂、断裂」，同样出自 rumpere。

entries.definition: Happening quickly and unexpectedly; the most general word for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「突然的」，是第一个义项最一般的说法，但不含「生硬」义。

entries.definition: Not anticipated, whether sudden or not.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「意外的、未料到的」，只强调没有预料，不强调速度快。

entries.definition: Short and rude in speech, often of a reply or a refusal.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「简短无礼的」，多指回答或拒绝，比 abrupt 更聚焦于言语的冷淡。

entries.definition: Rising or falling at a sharp angle, of a slope or price.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「陡峭的」，用于坡度或价格，与 abrupt 的地形义相近。

entries.definition: Done too quickly, without enough thought.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「仓促的、草率的」，强调做得太快而欠考虑，与 abrupt 的「突然」义不同。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb rumpere and the phrases abrupt commonly forms.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 rumpere，以及 abrupt 常见的搭配。

normal.en: rumpere is to break: abruptus is 'broken off'.
normal.cn: rumpere 是「折断」：abruptus 就是「被折断的」。

normal.en: ab- means away, so abrumpere is to break away or snap off.
normal.cn: ab- 意为「离开」，所以 abrumpere 是「折断、断掉」。

normal.en: Erupt and rupture belong to the same rumpere family.
normal.cn: erupt 与 rupture 都属于同一个 rumpere 词族。

normal.en: An abrupt end is a sentence snapped in the middle.
normal.cn: an abrupt end 就是一句话从中间被折断。

normal.en: An abrupt slope and an abrupt manner share the same jump.
normal.cn: 陡坡与唐突的态度，共享同一个「陡然一跳」。

abstract.en: Picture a stick broken in two: one half points up, one half points down, with no curve between.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被折成两截的木棍：一半朝上，一半朝下，中间没有弧线。

abstract.en: The break can happen in a conversation, a graph, a hillside, or a person's voice.
abstract.cn: 这道断口可以出现在对话里、曲线里、山壁上，也可以出现在人的语气里。

abstract.en: Whatever is abrupt has lost its joining part.
abstract.cn: 凡是 abrupt 的东西，都失去了中间那段衔接。

examples.en: The road ended in an abrupt drop to the valley.
examples.cn: 道路在一处陡然落向山谷的地方到了尽头。

examples.en: His abrupt tone told us the subject was closed.
examples.cn: 他生硬的语气告诉我们这个话题到此为止。

examples.en: There was an abrupt change of plan after lunch.
examples.cn: 午饭后计划发生了突然的变化。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe a line broken instead of bending: a sudden event, a stopped process, a steep slope, a blunt manner, a cold answer, a disjointed style, a sharp change, an untransitioned jump.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在描述一条被折断而不是弯过去的线：突然的事件、中断的过程、陡峭的坡、唐突的态度、冷淡的回答、生硬的文风、急剧的变化、缺过渡的跳跃。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line is snapped in two, leaving a hard edge with no curve.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线被折成两截，留下没有弧度的硬边。

branches.en: THE EVENT: an occurrence, a process or a change stops or jumps with no warning.
branches.cn: 事件线：一件事、一个过程或一次变化毫无预兆地停住或跳起。

branches.en: THE GROUND: a slope rises or falls at a sharp angle rather than gradually.
branches.cn: 地面线：坡面以很陡的角度升起或落下，而不是缓缓过渡。

branches.en: THE PERSON: speech and replies are cut short, and the cut feels cold or rude.
branches.cn: 人物线：话语与回答被剪短，这种剪断让人感到冷淡或无礼。

branches.en: THE STYLE: missing transitions make a text look broken into pieces.
branches.cn: 风格线：缺少衔接使文本看起来像被折成碎片。

branches.en: THE SEQUENCE: a narrative jumps from one scene to the next without a bridge.
branches.cn: 序列线：叙事从一个场景跳到下一个，中间没有桥。

senses.title: An ordered line of people or vehicles moving forward

senses.example: The whole town watched the religious procession pass the square.
senses.exampleCN: 全镇的人看着宗教游行经过广场。

senses.title: A continuous series of people or things
