senses.why: A marching line is also a sequence, since each person arrives after the one before, so the picture slides easily into any run of things arriving in turn.
senses.whyCN: 行进队伍本身就是一个序列：后一个人接着前一个人到来，因此这幅画面很自然地滑向「依次到来的一串事物」。

senses.title: The act of moving forward as a group in ritual
senses.definition: the act or ceremony of walking forward together in a set order, especially in church or funeral rites
senses.definitionCN: 按固定次序一起向前行走的动作或仪式，尤见于教堂礼仪与葬礼
senses.example: The choir began its slow procession down the aisle.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班开始沿着过道缓缓行进。
senses.why: Here the focus shifts from the line of people to the ritual act itself, which is why the word can name the walking as well as the walkers.
senses.whyCN: 这里重心从「那一列人」转到「行进这个仪式动作」，所以这个词既能指队伍，也能指列队行进的举动。

intro.en: Procession comes from a Latin verb meaning to go forward; the line of people is named after the movement, not the other way round.
intro.cn: procession 来自一个意为「向前走」的拉丁动词；先有「前行」这个动作，才用它来指排成行列的人。

items.en: Cedere meant to go, to withdraw or to yield, and it is the moving element inside many English words.
items.cn: cedere 意为走、退去、让出，是许多英语词里表示「移动」的那个成分。

items.en: The prefix pro- added forward to cedere, giving procedere, to go forward or advance.
items.cn: 前缀 pro- 给 cedere 加上了「向前」，构成 procedere，意为向前走、前进。

items.en: The noun processio named a going forward and later the ordered line of people making that advance.
items.cn: 名词 processio 指「向前行进」，后来也指排成次序完成这次行进的人群。

items.en: Old French kept the word as procession, meaning a ceremonial march, and passed it into English.
items.cn: 古法语沿用 procession 这一形式，指仪式性的行进，并把它传入英语。

items.en: English widened it from religious and funeral lines to any parade, then to any series arriving in turn.
items.cn: 英语把词义从宗教与送葬行列扩展到各种游行，再引申为依次到来的一连串事物。

note.en: The first group gathers words built on the same Latin verb of going; the second gathers words for organised walking and parades.
note.cn: 第一组收同一拉丁「走」动词上的词；第二组收表示有组织地行走与游行的词。

entries.definition: To go on or move forward, especially after a stop.
entries.definitionCN: 继续前行；在停顿之后继续进行。

entries.definition: A series of actions taken to reach a result.
entries.definitionCN: 为达到结果而采取的一系列行动。

entries.definition: An established or official way of doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 既定或正式的做法；程序。

entries.definition: To move back or away from a previous position.
entries.definitionCN: 后退；从原来的位置退去。

entries.definition: A public procession celebrating a special day.
entries.definitionCN: 为庆祝特定日子而举行的公开游行。

entries.definition: An organised walk by a group, often to protest.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织的集体行走，常指抗议游行。

entries.definition: A solemn procession, especially at a funeral.
entries.definitionCN: 庄严肃穆的行列，尤指送葬队伍。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin verb of going, and everything it means can be traced back to people moving forward in order.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在表示「走」的拉丁动词上，它的各种含义都能回溯到「人们有序地向前移动」。

normal.en: Cedere is the Latin verb to go; pro- pushes it forward, so procedere is simply to go forward.
normal.cn: cedere 是拉丁语「走」的动词，pro- 把它推向前，所以 procedere 就是「向前走」。

normal.en: Procession is the noun of that going forward, which is why it names the movement before it names the crowd.
normal.cn: procession 是「向前走」这个动作的名词形式，所以先指移动，再指做这件事的人群。

normal.en: Funeral and wedding processions use one word because both are ordered lines on the move.
normal.cn: 送葬与婚礼都用同一个词，因为两者都是行进中的有序队列。

normal.en: In procession means arranged in a line, a phrase that still holds the picture of people following one another.
normal.cn: in procession 意为排成队列，这个说法仍保留着人们一个跟着一个的画面。

normal.en: Process and proceed share the root, so all three keep the idea of stepping forward through stages.
normal.cn: process 与 proceed 同根，三者都保留着「一步步向前推进」的意思。

abstract.en: A procession turns separate bodies into one shape, because a line has a direction that no single walker owns.
abstract.cn: 行列把一个个身体合成一个形状，因为一条线的方向不属于任何单独的行进者。

abstract.en: Anything that arrives one after another can be seen as a procession, even when nobody is walking.
abstract.cn: 任何依次到来的东西都能被看成一列队伍，即使没有人在走。

abstract.en: The word suggests that order is visible: you know a procession is there because the line can be seen from far off.
abstract.cn: 这个词暗示秩序是可见的：远远看见那条线，就知道有一列队伍。

examples.en: The funeral procession moved slowly towards the church.
examples.cn: 送葬队伍缓缓向教堂行进。

examples.en: A procession of schoolchildren crossed the bridge in pairs.
examples.cn: 一队小学生两人一排地走过桥。

examples.en: The festival ended with a torchlight procession through the old town.
examples.cn: 节日以穿过老城区的火炬游行结束。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普若赛神」——一队人吹吹打打抬着神像往前走，像在赛神；记住 procession 是行列、游行队伍。

root: 拉丁语 pro-（向前）+ cedere（走、退让）→ procedere（前进）→ processio（行进、行列），经古法语 procession 进入英语；同族词多与「向前走、依次推进」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is people moving forward in order; from it come the public parade, the ritual act of walking, and the figurative series that arrives one by one.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是人们有次序地向前移动；由此分出公开游行、仪式性的列队行进，以及一个接一个到来的抽象序列。

intro.cn: 这个词由表示「走」的拉丁动词、它的前缀，以及两个把动作变成名词和形容词的词尾共同支撑。

senses.title: A person who cuts hair
senses.definition: a person whose job is to cut and trim hair, especially men's hair
senses.definitionCN: 以剪修头发为业的人，尤指给男性理发者

senses.why: English often names a shop by its worker, so the barber's came to mean the barber's shop.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用店员的称呼来指店铺，所以 the barber's 就表示理发店。

definition_zh: 坚持；持续；执意；存留；持久化
definition_en: to keep doing something despite difficulty, or to continue to exist beyond the expected time
core_image: 一个人站在原地不动，风一直吹，他始终没退一步。
scene: 他退烧之后，咳嗽又持续了三个星期。 The cough persisted for three weeks after the fever cleared.
sceneCN: 这里 persist 是「（症状）持续不退」（第 3 个义项：病症延续）；句意：退烧之后，咳嗽还持续了三周。场景要点：药瓶、日历上划掉的日期、仍在咳的人；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 坚持；持续；持久性
坚持不懈的；持续的；顽固的
持续地；固执地

senses.title: Keep going despite difficulty
senses.definition: to continue an effort even when it is hard or slow to succeed
senses.definitionCN: 即使困难或见效缓慢，仍继续努力
senses.example: She persisted with the experiment after four failed trials.
senses.exampleCN: 四次试验失败后，她仍坚持做这个实验。
senses.why: Latin sistere meant 'to stand firm, take a stand'. Persist is per- 'thoroughly' + sistere: to stand your ground all the way through.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 sistere 意为“站稳、站定”。persist 是 per-“彻底”+ sistere：从头到尾站住不退。

senses.title: Continue to exist
senses.definition: of a condition, practice, or thing, to continue to exist over time
senses.definitionCN: 指某种状况、做法或事物随时间继续存在
senses.example: The custom persists in rural areas.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗在农村地区仍然存在。
senses.why: The standing image is applied to existence itself: something that stands does not fall away, so it keeps being there.
senses.whyCN: “站住”的意象被用在存在本身：站住的东西不会倒掉，因此一直还在。

senses.title: Of a symptom: fail to clear
senses.definition: of an illness or symptom, to continue longer than expected
senses.definitionCN: 指疾病或症状持续的时间超过预期
senses.example: See a doctor if the fever persists for more than three days.
senses.exampleCN: 如果发烧持续超过三天，请就医。
senses.why: A symptom is something standing in the body that refuses to leave. The verb marks duration, not effort, which is why medical usage is so common.
senses.whyCN: 症状是站在身体里不肯走的东西。这个动词标记的是“时程”而非“努力”，所以医学用法很常见。

senses.title: Of a smell or trace: remain
senses.definition: of a smell, taste, impression, or mark, to remain after its source has gone
senses.definitionCN: 指气味、味道、印象或痕迹在来源消失后仍然留着
senses.example: The smell of smoke persisted in the curtains for days.
senses.exampleCN: 烟味在窗帘上留了好几天。
senses.why: The trace keeps standing in the material even after the fire is out. Persistence here is physical stubbornness.
senses.whyCN: 火灭了，痕迹仍站在布料里。这里的持续，是一种物理上的不肯走。

senses.title: Keep asking or doing, annoyingly
senses.definition: to continue doing or asking something in a way that others find hard to stop
senses.definitionCN: 以别人难以阻止的方式反复做或反复问
senses.example: He persisted in calling until she answered.
senses.exampleCN: 他一直打个不停，直到她接电话。
senses.why: The same standing firm can be read from outside as refusal to take no for an answer. The virtue turns into a nuisance.
senses.whyCN: 同一个“站住”，从外面看就是不肯接受“不”。美德由此变成了烦扰。

senses.title: Of a belief or institution: survive
senses.titleCN: 观念延续：穿过年代还在
senses.definition: of a belief, institution, or idea, to survive over a long time
senses.definitionCN: 指信念、制度或观念长期存续下来
senses.example: The belief persisted long after the empire fell.
senses.exampleCN: 帝国灭亡很久之后，这种信仰仍然延续。
senses.why: Institutions stand longer than the people who hold them up. Persistence becomes a measure of historical survival.
senses.whyCN: 制度比撑着它的人站得更久。持续由此成为衡量历史存活的尺度。

senses.title: Computing: store data permanently
senses.definition: of data, to remain stored after a program or device stops running
senses.definitionCN: 指数据在程序或设备停止运行后仍然保留
senses.example: The settings persist even after a restart.
senses.exampleCN: 即使重启，设置也会保留。
senses.why: Memory that vanishes is data that could not stand. Persistent storage is the technical version of 'still standing after the power goes off'.
senses.whyCN: 一断电就消失的记忆，是站不住的数据。持久化存储，就是“断电后仍站着”的技术版本。

senses.title: Insist stubbornly against advice
senses.definition: to continue in a course of action in spite of warnings or good advice
senses.definitionCN: 不顾警告或善意劝告，继续照自己的做法行事
senses.example: He persisted in driving despite the closed-road signs.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管有封路标志，他仍执意开车。
senses.why: Standing firm with no reason to stand is stubbornness. The word does not judge by itself; the context decides whether to praise or blame.
senses.whyCN: 没有理由还站着，就是固执。这个词本身不作评判，是语境决定该夸还是该责。

intro.en: Persist is Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'to stand firm', from the same Indo-European root as stand. The core is not effort but posture: staying on your feet.
intro.cn: persist 是拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，与 stand 同出一个印欧词根。它的核心不是努力，而是姿态：站住不倒。

items.en: The root *sta- gives Latin stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and English stand, stable, statue, and constant.
items.cn: 词根 *sta- 衍生出拉丁语 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”，以及英语 stand、stable、statue、constant。

items.en: Sistere meant 'to cause to stand, place, stop'. Its frequentative form was used for holding a position, which is the seed of 'persist'.
items.cn: sistere 意为“使站住、安置、停住”。它的反复形式用于“守住位置”，这正是 persist 的种子。

items.en: Persistere combined per- 'through, thoroughly' with sistere: 'to continue standing, persevere, persist'.
items.cn: persistere 把 per-“贯穿、彻底”与 sistere 结合：“一直站住、坚持、持续”。

items.en: English records persist in the 1530s, first of persons continuing in a course, then of things continuing to exist.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪 30 年代记录 persist，先指人继续走某条路，后指事物继续存在。

items.en: The medical sense of a symptom that will not clear and the physical sense of a smell that remains both grow from the same 'still standing' image.
items.cn: 症状不退的医学义与气味残留的物理义，都从同一个“仍站着”的意象长出来。

items.en: Persistent storage and persistent data apply the old verb to memory that survives a restart. Persistence becomes a technical property.
items.cn: persistent storage 与 persistent data 把这个老动词用在重启后仍存活的内存上。持续由此成为一种技术属性。

note.en: The first group is the persist family plus the Latin verb behind it; the second separates near-synonyms by what exactly keeps going.
note.cn: 第一组是 persist 词族及其背后的拉丁动词；第二组按“究竟是什么在继续”区分近义词。

entries.definition: the quality of continuing despite difficulty, or of lasting. It is the noun of persist.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍继续的品质，或持久性。它是 persist 的名词。

entries.definition: continuing firmly or lasting a long time. It describes the person or thing, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的。它描述人或物，而非动作。

entries.definition: a rarer synonym of persistence, used especially in older technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: persistence 的较罕见同义词，多用于较早的技术文献。

entries.definition: not lasting, used of chemicals that break down quickly and of network connections that close after use.
entries.definitionCN: 不持久的，用于快速降解的化学品，或用完即关闭的网络连接。

entries.definition: to keep trying despite difficulty. It is close to persist but almost always about deliberate human effort toward a goal.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管困难仍不断尝试。它与 persist 接近，但几乎总指人为目标付出的努力。

entries.definition: to keep happening or doing without stopping. It is the neutral word and carries no idea of resistance.
entries.definitionCN: 不停地继续发生或做。它最中性，不含抵抗之意。

entries.definition: to suffer something difficult patiently, or to last a long time. It adds the weight of suffering or durability.
entries.definitionCN: 耐心承受艰难，或长久存在。它加了受苦或耐久的分量。

entries.definition: to stay longer than expected, often unwillingly. It is used of smells, illness, and people who should go.
entries.definitionCN: 比预期停留更久，常含不愿离开。它用于气味、疾病与该走的人。

entries.definition: to demand something firmly. It is about a claim or demand, while persist is about continuing an action.
entries.definitionCN: 坚决要求。它关于主张或要求，而 persist 关于继续行动。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Latin per- 'thoroughly' + sistere 'stand firm', from PIE *sta- 'stand'. Family words persistence, persistent, persistently; relatives stand, stable, statue, constant.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：拉丁语 per-“彻底”+ sistere“站稳”，源自原始印欧语 *sta-“站”。词族为 persistence、persistent、persistently；亲属词 stand、stable、statue、constant。

normal.en: Sistere is 'stand firm'; persist is standing firm all the way through.
normal.cn: sistere 是“站稳”；persist 就是从头到尾一直站稳。

normal.en: Stand, stable, statue, constant, persist: one *sta- family of standing.
normal.cn: stand、stable、statue、constant、persist：同一个 *sta-“站立”家族。

normal.en: A persistent cough is a cough that will not stand down.
normal.cn: persistent cough 就是不肯“退下”的咳嗽。

normal.en: Persistent data is data still standing after the power is cut.
normal.cn: persistent data 就是断电后仍站着的数据。

normal.en: Persist in and persist with are both about refusing to leave the spot.
normal.cn: persist in 与 persist with，都是不肯离开那个位置。

abstract.en: Persistence is often just the decision to remain where the difficulty is.
abstract.cn: 坚持，常常只是决定留在困难所在的那个地方。

abstract.en: What persists shapes the world more than what is intense.
abstract.cn: 留下来的东西，比强烈的东西更能塑造世界。

abstract.en: To persist is to make time your ally rather than your judge.
abstract.cn: 坚持，就是把时间变成盟友，而不是法官。

examples.en: The team persisted through two years of rejected applications.
examples.cn: 团队在两年申请被拒的情况下仍坚持下来。

examples.en: Old farming methods persist in the valley.
examples.cn: 古老的耕作方式在山谷里仍然延续。

examples.en: The rash persisted after the course of antibiotics ended.
examples.cn: 抗生素疗程结束后，皮疹仍未消退。

dict_mnemonic.text: “破吸石”——破吸盘还能吸在石头上不掉，风再大也不松 → persist 坚持、持续

root: 源自拉丁语 persistere“一直站住、坚持”，由 per-“贯穿、彻底”+ sistere“站稳、使站住”构成；sistere 与 stare“站”同出原始印欧语 *sta-“站”，故与 stand、stable、statue、constant 同源。核心是“站住不倒”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of persist, all one posture: something stays standing when it could have fallen, stopped, or gone away.
sensesIntro.cn: persist 的八个义项是同一个姿态：本可以倒下、停止或离开的东西，仍然站着。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure standing in wind, feet planted, not moving back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在风里，双脚钉住，不退一步。

branches.en: WILL: effort and stubbornness are the same posture seen from inside and from outside.
branches.cn: 意志：努力与固执，是同一个姿态从里面和外面看的样子。

branches.en: EXISTENCE: a custom or belief stands longer than the people holding it up.
branches.cn: 存在：习俗或信仰，比撑着它的人站得更久。

branches.en: TRACES: a symptom and a smell both stay in the body or the cloth after their cause is gone.
branches.cn: 痕迹：症状与气味，都在成因消失后仍留在身体或布料里。

branches.en: PRESSURE: asking again and again is standing firm in someone else's doorway.
branches.cn: 压力：一遍遍追问，就是在别人的门口站住不走。

branches.en: MACHINES: persistent storage is memory that survives the power being switched off.
branches.cn: 机器：持久化存储，是断电后仍存活的内存。

intro.en: Persist's family is built on Latin sistere 'to stand firm'. Suffixes mark the state, the person or thing, and the manner; non- removes the lasting.
intro.cn: persist 的词族建立在拉丁语 sistere“站稳”上。后缀标记状态、人与方式；non- 则取消“持久”。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are stare 'to stand', sistere 'cause to stand', and persistere 'continue standing'. The whole family belongs to PIE *sta-.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是 stare“站”、sistere“使站住”与 persistere“继续站住”。整个词族都属于原始印欧语 *sta-。

items.meaning: the fact or quality of continuing or lasting
items.meaningCN: 继续或持久的事实或品质（-ence 构成状态名词）
items.example: Her persistence eventually won the funding.
items.exampleCN: 她的坚持最终争取到了资助。

items.meaning: continuing firmly or lasting a long time
items.meaningCN: 坚持不懈的；持续时间长的（-ent 构成形容词）
items.exampleCN: 持续不断的雨取消了比赛。

items.meaning: in a continuing or stubborn manner
items.meaningCN: 持续地；固执地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: a rarer form of persistence, chiefly technical
items.meaningCN: persistence 的较罕见形式，主要用于技术文献
items.example: The persistency of the pesticide was measured in soil.
items.exampleCN: 这种农药在土壤中的持久性被测定了。

items.meaning: not lasting long in the environment or in memory
items.meaningCN: 在环境中或内存中不长久留存的（non- 表示否定）
items.example: Non-persistent chemicals break down within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 非持久性化学品在几周内降解。

items.meaning: to continue doing something, often against advice
items.meaningCN: 继续做某事，常指不听劝（in 标记活动）
items.example: They persisted in asking for a written answer.
items.exampleCN: 他们执意要求一份书面答复。

items.meaning: to continue with a task or plan
items.meaningCN: 继续某项工作或计划（with 标记对象）
items.example: She persisted with the treatment for a full year.
items.exampleCN: 她坚持治疗了整整一年。

items.meaning: a person who keeps committing offences
items.meaningCN: 反复犯罪的人（法律术语）
items.example: He was classified as a persistent offender.

items.meaning: memory that keeps data after power is removed
items.meaningCN: 断电后仍保存数据的存储（计算机术语）
items.example: The logs are written to persistent storage.
items.exampleCN: 日志被写入持久化存储。

items.meaning: the way an image stays on the retina briefly and makes film appear to move
items.meaningCN: 图像在视网膜上短暂停留、使电影看起来在动的现象
items.example: Animation relies on the persistence of vision.

latinEntries.meaning: to cause to stand, place, stop

definition_zh: 必要性；必需品；贫困；必然性；迫不得已
definition_en: the state of being necessary; something that cannot be done without; also poverty or unavoidable need
core_image: 一只空水壶立在桌上，旁边是一张写满“必须”的清单，第一行写着水，后面才是别的。
scene: 救援队在出发前清点物资，队长说，干净的水要排在最前面。 Clean water is the first necessity for the team.
sceneCN: 这里 necessity 是“不可或缺的东西、必需品”（第 2 个义项）；句意：干净的水是队伍最首要的必需品；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 必要性；必需品；贫困；必然性；（不得已的）需要

derivatives.zh: 必要的；必然的
必然地；必定
使成为必要；需要
不必要的；多余的

senses.title: The state of being needed
senses.definition: the condition of being required or indispensable for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为达成某目的而被需要、不可缺的状态
senses.example: The report argues the necessity of a second runway at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 报告论证了机场修建第二条跑道的必要性。
senses.why: This is the abstract quality, not the object: it answers the question 'why must this be done?' rather than 'what do we need?'
senses.whyCN: 这是抽象的性质，而不是具体的东西：它回答“为什么非做不可”，而不是“我们需要什么”。

senses.title: Something you cannot do without
senses.titleCN: 必需品：清单上排第一的东西
senses.definition: an item that is essential for living or for a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 维持生活或完成某项活动所必需的东西
senses.example: The clinic lacks the basic necessities: clean water, gloves, and bandages.
senses.exampleCN: 诊所缺少基本必需品：干净的水、手套和绷带。
senses.why: The abstract quality turns concrete: if something is necessary, then the thing itself can be called a necessity and counted in a list.
senses.whyCN: 抽象性质具体化了：如果某物是必要的，那么该物本身就可以被称为 necessity，并能列进清单里点算。

senses.title: Hardship and poverty
senses.titleCN: 贫困窘迫：被“必需”逼到角落
senses.definition: the condition of extreme need or poverty, especially when money is short
senses.definitionCN: 极度匮乏或贫困的处境，尤指缺钱的状况
senses.example: Many families were driven by necessity to sell their tools.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家庭因贫困所迫卖掉了工具。
senses.why: When needs cannot be met, necessity stops meaning 'requirement' and starts naming the pressure itself, which is close to want and hardship.
senses.whyCN: 当需求无法满足时，necessity 就不再表示“要求”，而开始指那种压力本身，接近匮乏与困苦。

senses.title: Logical inevitability
senses.titleCN: 逻辑必然：前提逼出结论
senses.definition: the quality of following unavoidably from given premises or laws
senses.definitionCN: 由既定前提或规律不可回避地推出的性质
senses.example: The necessity of the conclusion follows from the two premises.
senses.exampleCN: 该结论的必然性由那两个前提推出。
senses.why: In logic the word marks that a step cannot fail: if the premises hold, the conclusion has no alternative.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑中，这个词标出某一步不可能失手：前提成立，结论就别无选择。

senses.title: What cannot be otherwise
senses.titleCN: 不可避免：事情只能这样发生
senses.definition: the character of an event that could not have happened differently
senses.definitionCN: 某事无法以别的方式发生的性质
senses.example: The historian describes the collapse as a necessity rather than an accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学家把那次崩溃描述为必然，而非意外。
senses.why: Here necessity is applied to events, not to logic: the claim is that conditions left no room for another outcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里 necessity 用于事件而非逻辑：主张是条件没有给别的结果留余地。

senses.title: The means of living
senses.titleCN: 生计所需：过日子离不开的
senses.definition: the conditions or resources required to maintain life
senses.definitionCN: 维持生活所必需的条件或资源
senses.example: The workers asked for enough wages to cover the necessities of life.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们要求足够的工资来支付生活必需品。
senses.why: The plural ties the word to the household: air, water, food, and shelter are necessities because life cannot continue without them.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式把这个词拴在家计上：空气、水、食物和住所之所以是 necessities，是因为缺了它们生活无法继续。

senses.title: Only because one must
senses.titleCN: 迫不得已：不是想，而是不得不
senses.definition: the pressure of circumstances that forces an action one would not otherwise choose
senses.definitionCN: 迫使人们做出本不会选择的行为的处境压力
senses.example: Out of necessity, she took the night shift and gave up her classes.
senses.exampleCN: 迫不得已，她接了夜班，放弃了课程。
senses.why: In the phrase out of necessity, the word names the cause of an unwanted choice: the action is explained, not praised.
senses.whyCN: 在“出于无奈”这一说法里，这个词说明一个并不想要的选择的原因：它是在解释行为，而不是在赞美行为。

senses.title: A category in philosophy
senses.titleCN: 哲学范畴：必然与偶然相对
senses.definition: the philosophical category of what must be, as opposed to what happens by chance
senses.definitionCN: 哲学上“必定如此”的范畴，与偶然相对
senses.example: The dialogue contrasts necessity with chance in the order of the universe.
senses.exampleCN: 这段对话在宇宙秩序中把必然与偶然对照起来。
senses.why: Philosophy turns the everyday pressure into a category: some things are said to be necessary in themselves, not merely needed by someone.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把日常的压力提升为一个范畴：有些事物被说成自身必然，而不只是被某人需要。

intro.en: Necessity comes from Latin necessitas, from necesse, 'unavoidable'. The internal structure of necesse is disputed, so the word's deeper root is best marked as uncertain.
intro.cn: necessity 来自拉丁语 necessitas，出自 necesse“不可避免”。necesse 的内部结构存在争议，因此更深的词根应标为来源不确定。

items.en: Necesse meant unavoidable or indispensable. It was already used both for logical compulsion and for the pressure of circumstances.
items.cn: necesse 意为“不可避免的、不可或缺的”，当时既用于逻辑强制，也用于处境的压力。

items.en: The noun added the senses of compulsion, need, poverty, and bonds of duty. It could name both an inner must and an outer shortage.
items.cn: 名词形式增加了强制、需要、贫困与义务约束等义，既能指内在的“必须”，也能指外在的匮乏。

items.en: The commonly repeated split ne- 'not' plus cedere 'yield' would mean 'not yielding'. This is a plausible reconstruction, not a confirmed derivation, so it is marked uncertain.
items.cn: 常见的拆解是 ne-“不”加 cedere“让步”，意为“不让步”。这是一种合理的重构，并非已确认的派生，故标为来源不确定。

items.en: Old French necessité carried the senses of need, compulsion, and want. English borrowed the word in the 14th century through French.
items.cn: 古法语 necessité 带有需要、强制与匮乏等义。英语于 14 世纪经法语借入该词。

items.en: English necessity first covered compulsion and need, then widened to include indispensable objects and the philosophical category of inevitability.
items.cn: 英语 necessity 最初涵盖强制与需要，随后扩展到不可或缺的物品，以及哲学上的必然性范畴。

items.en: The plural necessities settled into household and economic language, giving phrases such as daily necessities and bare necessities.
items.cn: 复数 necessities 固定于家庭与经济语境，形成 daily necessities、bare necessities 等说法。

note.en: The first group is the necessary word family; the second compares words for needs and for inevitability.
note.cn: 第一组是 necessary 的词族；第二组比较表示“需要”与“必然”的词。

entries.definition: required, or certain to happen. It describes a thing or a conclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 必需的，或必定发生的；描述事物或结论。

entries.definition: to make something necessary. It names the cause, not the need.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要；命名的是原因，不是需要本身。

entries.definition: in every case, or as a logical consequence. It often appears in negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 在所有情况下，或作为逻辑结果；常出现在否定句中。

entries.definition: absolutely important or basic. It grades importance but does not claim that something cannot be omitted.
entries.definitionCN: 绝对重要或基本的；它给重要性分级，但不宣称不可省略。

entries.definition: something officially demanded or needed for a purpose. It comes from a rule or authority.
entries.definitionCN: 为某目的被正式要求或需要之物；来源于规定或权威。

entries.definition: the quality of being impossible to avoid. It stresses the future, while necessity can be logical.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免的性质；侧重未来，而 necessity 可以是逻辑上的。

entries.definition: the state of lacking money or goods. It is one concrete sense of necessity, not the whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 缺钱或缺物的状态；它只是 necessity 的一个具体义项。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin necesse, unavoidable, plus the noun suffix -itas, which became English -ity. The word names the 'must' itself.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 necesse“不可避免”，加名词后缀 -itas（英语作 -ity）。这个词命名的是“必须”本身。

normal.en: A necessity is whatever stands first on the list when everything else is crossed out.
normal.cn: necessity 就是把其他都划掉后仍留在清单第一行的东西。

normal.en: Out of necessity means the choice was made by circumstances, not by preference.
normal.cn: out of necessity 意味着选择是处境做的，不是偏好做的。

normal.en: Water, food, shelter: plural necessities are the household version of the abstract word.
normal.cn: 水、食物、住所：复数的 necessities 就是这个词的家计版本。

normal.en: In a proof, necessity is the step that cannot be skipped.
normal.cn: 在证明里，necessity 就是那步不能跳过的地方。

normal.en: Necessity and necessary share one spine; only the ending changes the job.
normal.cn: necessity 与 necessary 共享同一根脊梁，只是词尾改变了词性。

abstract.en: Necessity is a mirror held up to desire: it shows how much of what we call 'must' is only 'would like'.
abstract.cn: necessity 是一面照向欲望的镜子：它照出我们称为“必须”的东西里，有多少其实只是“想要”。

abstract.en: Every claim of necessity removes an option, and whoever defines necessity controls the choices of others.
abstract.cn: 每一次“必然”的宣称都在删掉一个选项；谁定义必然，谁就掌握了他人的选择。

abstract.en: The word ties a physical shortage to a logical conclusion, as if what is missing could prove what must be.
abstract.cn: 这个词把物质匮乏与逻辑结论绑在一起，仿佛缺什么就能证明什么必然如此。

examples.en: The engineers questioned the necessity of the extra tower, given the new safety system.
examples.cn: 鉴于新的安全系统，工程师们质疑了额外那座塔的必要性。

examples.en: In the drought year, water became a necessity that the town rationed by the bucket.
examples.cn: 干旱那年，水成了小镇按桶配给的必需品。

examples.en: Of necessity, the team shipped the simple version first and saved the refinements for later.
examples.cn: 不得已之下，团队先交付了简单版本，把改进留到以后。

dict_mnemonic.text: ne（不）+ cess（退）+ ity——一步也不退，就是“必要、必然”；不退的东西就是必需品。

root: 源自拉丁语 necessitas（必然、需要、困乏），出自 necesse（不可避免的）；其更早的词根拆解存在争议，通常的说法是 ne-“不”加 cedere“让步”，但未获确证，应视为重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of necessity, from abstract requirement to concrete goods, hardship, and logical compulsion. The shared core is a door that will not open: something that cannot be refused, omitted, or otherwise arranged.
sensesIntro.cn: necessity 的八个义项，从抽象要求到具体物品、贫困与逻辑强制。共同的核心是一扇打不开的门：某个东西无法被拒绝、省略或另行安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty water jug beside a list whose first line reads water, with everything else below it.
core.cn: 核心意象：空水壶旁一张清单，第一行写着水，其余都排在下面。

chain: ENGLISH NECESSITY THE STATE OF BEING NEEDED

branches.en: COMPULSION: a required condition and a forced conclusion both leave no alternative.
branches.cn: 强制：必需的条件与被迫的结论，都不留别的可能。

branches.en: THE THING NEEDED: from a clinic's clean water to a household's means of living.
branches.cn: 被需要之物：从诊所的干净水到家庭的生计来源。

branches.en: PRESSURE: poverty and 'out of necessity' both describe circumstances forcing a choice.
branches.cn: 压力：贫困与“迫不得已”都描述处境逼迫下的选择。

branches.en: EVENTS THAT COULD NOT DIFFER: history read as inevitability rather than accident.
branches.cn: 无法两样的事件：把历史读成必然而非偶然。

branches.en: A PHILOSOPHICAL CATEGORY: necessity set against chance in the order of things.
branches.cn: 哲学范畴：在万物秩序中把必然与偶然对置。

intro.en: Necessity is Latin necesse plus -ity, the noun suffix from -itas. The family runs through necessary, necessitate, and necessarily, with un- forming the negative.
intro.cn: necessity 是拉丁语 necesse 加 -ity（源自 -itas 的名词后缀）。词族包括 necessary、necessitate、necessarily，并用 un- 构成否定。

latinIntro.en: The base is necesse, unavoidable, with the noun necessitas and the adjective necessarius. The deeper root of necesse is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是 necesse“不可避免”，名词 necessitas，形容词 necessarius。necesse 的更早词根存在争议。

items.example: A visa is necessary for entry into the country.

items.meaning: the state of being needed, or the thing needed
items.example: The war turned bread into a daily necessity.
items.exampleCN: 战争让面包成了日常必需品。

items.meaning: in every case, or by logical consequence
items.example: A higher price does not necessarily mean better quality.
items.exampleCN: 价格更高并不必然意味着质量更好。

items.example: The repair will necessitate closing the road for a week.
items.exampleCN: 这项维修将使道路必须关闭一周。

items.example: The extra form added an unnecessary delay.
items.exampleCN: 那张额外的表格造成了不必要的延误。

items.meaning: things needed for a purpose, especially in law and trade
items.meaningCN: 所需物品，尤用于法律与贸易语境
items.example: The contract covered the necessaries for the voyage.
items.exampleCN: 合同涵盖了此次航行所需的物品。

items.meaning: poor or needy; in urgent want
items.example: The fund was set up for necessitous families.
items.exampleCN: 这项基金是为贫困家庭设立的。

items.meaning: the goods needed for daily life
items.example: The shelter stores blankets and other necessities.
items.exampleCN: 收容所存放毯子和其他生活必需品。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 不可避免的；不可或缺的

definition_zh: 恶习；邪恶；（机械）台钳；副职（前缀）
definition_en: a bad habit or immoral conduct, and, in compounds, a deputy
core_image: 老虎机旁的手一直不肯离开拉杆
scene: 社区讲座上，老师提醒家长别把赌博当成小事。 The talk warned that gambling is a costly vice for many families.
sceneCN: 这里 vice 是「恶习」（第 1 个义项：不良的习惯或不道德的行为）；句意为讲座警告赌博是许多家庭负担沉重的恶习。老虎机旁不肯放手的那只手就是这个词的画面。

derivatives.zh: 加后缀 -ious 构成，义为「凶恶的；恶毒的」
由 vicious 加 -ly 构成，义为「凶恶地」
拉丁短语，义为「反之亦然」

senses.title: A bad habit
senses.definition: a habit that is bad for the person who has it
senses.definitionCN: 对本人有害的习惯
senses.example: The talk warned that gambling is a vice that ruins families.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座警告赌博是一种毁掉家庭的恶习。
senses.why: Latin vitium named a flaw or a fault, and a habit can be exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vitium 指缺陷或过错，而习惯恰恰可能就是一个缺陷。

senses.title: Immoral conduct in general
senses.definition: wicked or immoral behaviour, especially in public life
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指公共生活中的邪恶或不道德行为
senses.example: The novel shows a city sinking into vice.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说写一座城市如何陷入堕落。
senses.why: A single flaw, repeated across a whole society, becomes a general word for wickedness.
senses.whyCN: 单个缺陷若在一整个社会反复出现，就成了泛指邪恶的词。

senses.title: A gripping tool on a workbench
senses.definition: a tool with two jaws that hold a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 用两个钳口夹住工件的工作台工具
senses.example: Clamp the wood in a vice before you saw it.
senses.exampleCN: 锯之前先把木头夹在台钳里。
senses.why: The jaws of the tool close like a grip, and English borrowed the name from the same Latin word for a clamping device.
senses.whyCN: 钳口像握住一样合拢，英语从同一个表示夹持器具的拉丁词借来了这个名字。

senses.title: A deputy in a title
senses.definition: a person next in rank, used in compounds such as vice president
senses.definitionCN: 职级仅次于正职的人，用于 vice president 这类复合词中
senses.example: The vice president chaired the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 副总裁主持了会议。
senses.why: Latin vice meant in place of, so a vice president stands in place of the president.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 vice 意为「代替」，所以 vice president 就是在总统（总裁）之时代行其职的人。

senses.title: A small weakness treated fondly
senses.definition: a small fault that people joke about rather than condemn
senses.definitionCN: 人们拿来打趣而不是谴责的小毛病
senses.example: Chocolate is my only vice.
senses.exampleCN: 巧克力是我唯一的嗜好。
senses.why: Once a moral word weakens, it can be used lightly about a harmless fondness.
senses.whyCN: 一个道德意味的词一旦变弱，就能轻松地用来指无伤大雅的偏好。

intro.en: Two Latin words lie behind vice: vitium, a fault, and vice, in place of.
intro.cn: vice 背后有两个拉丁词：vitium（过错）与 vice（代替）。

items.en: Vitium meant a defect, a fault, or a moral flaw.
items.cn: vitium 意为缺陷、过错或道德上的瑕疵。

items.en: French vice narrowed the word to a bad habit in daily life.
items.cn: 法语 vice 把词义收窄为日常生活中的恶习。

items.en: English used vice for a moral fault and for a gripping tool.
items.cn: 中世纪英语以 vice 既指道德上的过错，也指夹持的工具。

items.en: The separate Latin word vice meant in place of, as in vice consul.
items.cn: 另一个拉丁词 vice 意为「代替」，如 vice consul（副领事）。

items.en: Both strands meet in modern English: vice squad and vice president.
items.cn: 两支在现代英语里并存：vice squad（扫黄缉毒队）与 vice president（副总统）。

note.en: The first group holds the vice family, the second the moral words around it.
note.cn: 第一组是 vice 词族，第二组是围绕它的道德类词。

normalIntro.en: The bad habit and the deputy share a sound but not a history; keep the two strands apart.
normalIntro.cn: 「恶习」与「副职」读音相同却来源不同，要把两条线分开记。

normal.en: Advice and device contain vice by accident: they come from other roots.
normal.cn: advice 与 device 只是碰巧含 vice，来源不同。

normal.en: Vicious comes from vice, but a vice president does not.
normal.cn: vicious 来自「恶习」，vice president 则来自「代替」。

normal.en: A rule of thumb: vice before a title means deputy.
normal.cn: 一条经验：vice 放在头衔前就是「副」。

normal.en: The plural is vices, with the e kept.
normal.cn: 复数是 vices，保留 e。

normal.en: Latin vice meant in place of, as in vicarious.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 vice 意为代替，如 vicarious 一词中的含义。

abstract.en: See a hand that will not leave the lever of a slot machine.
abstract.cn: 想一只不肯离开老虎机拉杆的手。

abstract.en: Picture two steel jaws shutting on a plank.
abstract.cn: 想两个钢钳口夹住一块木板。

abstract.en: Think of a deputy who sits in the chief chair when the chief is away.
abstract.cn: 想一把手不在时坐在其位上的副手。

examples.en: Smoking is a vice many people struggle to give up.
examples.cn: 吸烟是许多人难以戒掉的恶习。

examples.en: She was appointed vice president of the company.
examples.cn: 她被任命为公司的副总裁。

examples.en: He fixed the shelf by holding the board in a vice.
examples.cn: 他用台钳夹住木板来修好了架子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外死」——熬夜刷手机这习惯，把身体往外死拖，是明摆的恶习。

root: 拉丁语 vitium（缺陷）→ 法语 vice（恶习）；另拉丁语 vice（代替）→ vice president（副职）

sensesIntro.en: One short word holds a fault, a wicked city, a workbench clamp, a deputy, and a joke about chocolate.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个短词里装着过错、堕落的城市、台钳、副职，还有一句拿巧克力打趣的话。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that cannot let go of a lever.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只放不下拉杆的手。

branches.en: The habit branch: gambling that ruins a family.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：毁掉家庭的赌博。

branches.en: The city branch: a town sinking into vice.
branches.cn: 城市分支：陷入堕落的小城。

branches.en: The bench branch: wood held in a vice.
branches.cn: 工作台分支：台钳夹住的木头。

branches.en: The deputy branch: the vice president in the chair.
branches.cn: 副职分支：坐在主位上的副总统。

branches.en: The joke branch: chocolate as my only vice.
branches.cn: 打趣分支：巧克力是我唯一的嗜好。

intro.en: The stem viti- (fault) built vicious; the separate Latin vice (in place of) built the deputy compounds.
intro.cn: 词干 viti-（过错）构成 vicious，另一个拉丁词 vice（代替）构成表副职的复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vitium and Latin vice look identical in English but are two different words with different relatives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vitium 与拉丁语 vice 在英语里写法相同，却是两个不同的词，亲属也不同。

items.example: A vice consul stands below the consul.
Vice versa means the order is turned.
items.exampleCN: vice versa 意为顺序反过来了。

items.example: Virtue and vice are an old pair.
items.exampleCN: 善与恶是一对古老的搭配。

items.example: Device has no link to vice.
items.exampleCN: device 与 vice 没有词源关系。

items.example: Advice comes from a different root.
Debt can become a vicious circle.
items.exampleCN: 债务可能变成恶性循环。
